children.translated_text: <s>Pāramitāsamāsa</s> (Compendium of the Perfections)
1. <s>Dānapāramitāsamāsa</s> (Summary of the Perfection of Giving)
Homage to the <s>Buddha</s>!
One who desires to ascend to the state of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, having taken refuge with devotion in the Three Jewels (<s>Ratnatraya</s>),

children.text: bodhau nidhāyāvicalaṃ manaśca kuryāt parātmavyatihāram ādau // Ps_1.1 //
children.translated_text: and having placed the mind unwaveringly upon <s>Bodhi</s> (awakening), should first practice the exchange of self and other.

children.text: tataḥ paraṃ dānavidhau prayogaḥ kāryastathā lokahitonmukhena /
children.translated_text: Thereafter, one who is intent on the welfare of the world should make effort in the method of giving,

children.text: yathā svagātrāṇyapi yācitasya na yogasaṃkocavirūpatā syāt // Ps_1.2 //
children.translated_text: so that even when his own limbs are requested, there would be no disfigurement through the contraction of [his] practice.

children.text: mātsaryadoṣopacayāya yat syān na tyāgacittaṃ paribṛṃhayed vā /
children.translated_text: Whatever would lead to the increase of the fault of avarice (<s>mātsarya</s>), or would not nourish the mind of renunciation —
that the <s>bodhisattva</s> should indeed renounce: the obstacle disguised as possession.

children.text: tad bodhisattvaḥ katham ādadīta ratnaṃ dhanaṃ vā divi vāpi rājyam /
children.translated_text: How then could a <s>bodhisattva</s> accept jewels, wealth, or even sovereignty in heaven,
which, being adept at opposing the mind of renunciation, creates an obstruction to the path of complete awakening (<s>Saṃbodhi</s>)?

children.text: saṃsmṛtya caryātiśayaṃ munīnāṃ tadunmukhīṃ svāmapi ca pratijñām /
children.translated_text: Remembering the extraordinary conduct of the sages (<s>munis</s>) and his own vow directed toward that,
for the purpose of restraining attachment to possessions, he should cultivate these wholesome reflections in his mind:

children.text: yadā nisṛṣṭo jagate mayāyaṃ kāyo 'pī tattyāgakṛto 'pi dharmaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'When this body has been given by me to the world, and the <s>dharma</s> of that renunciation has been performed,

children.text: bāhye tadā vastuni saṅgacittaṃ na me gajasnānam ivānurūpam // Ps_1.6 //
children.translated_text: then attachment of mind to external things would be no more fitting for me than an elephant's bath.'
'Let those who desire flesh take this flesh; let one who seeks marrow extract even the marrow.

children.text: ahaṃ hi lokārthamidaṃ bibharmi śarīrakaṃ kiṃ bata vastu bāhyam // Ps_1.7 //
children.translated_text: For I bear this little body for the sake of the world — how much more so external things!'
'Just as people take the bark, leaves, flowers, and so forth of a medicinal tree,

children.text: madīyamete 'paharanti ceti naivaṃ vikalpāḥ samudācaranti // Ps_1.8 //
children.translated_text: and the thought "these people are taking what is mine" does not occur in such distinctions —'

children.text: tathaiva lokārthasamudyatena svalpo 'pi kāryo na mayā vikalpaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'So likewise, by me who am engaged in the welfare of the world, not even the slightest discrimination should be made

children.text: duḥkhe kṛtaghne satatāśucau ca dehe parasmāyupayujyamāne // Ps_1.9 //
children.translated_text: regarding this body — [which is full of] suffering, ungrateful, and ever-impure — when it is being used for the benefit of another.'

children.text: ādhyātmike caiva mahījalādye bāhye mahābhūtagaṇe ca tulye /
children.translated_text: 'When the internal [elements] — earth, water, and so forth — and the external group of great elements are equal,

children.text: idaṃ mamedaṃ na mameti ko 'yam ajñānapaṅkāṅkavidhirmayāpi // Ps_1.10 //
children.translated_text: what is this way of marking "this is mine, this is not mine" — a stamp of the mud of ignorance — even by me?'

children.text: gṛhṇīta gātrāṇyapi me yatheṣṭaṃ mā kārṣurasmin parakīyabuddhim /
children.translated_text: 'Take even my limbs as you wish — do not regard this [body] as belonging to another!

children.text: yuṣmākameva svamidaṃ kimarthaṃ nātmābhimāno mama kaścidatra // Ps_1.11 //
children.translated_text: This is your very own — why [hesitate]? I have no self-conceit whatsoever here.'
He whose wondrous reflections, in conformity with the state of a perfect <s>Buddha</s>, arise constantly —

children.text: taṃ bodhisattvātiśayaṃ vadanti buddhā mahāsattvamacintyasattvāḥ // Ps_1.12 //
children.translated_text: the <s>Buddhas</s>, great beings of inconceivable nature, call him an extraordinary <s>bodhisattva</s>, a <s>mahāsattva</s> (great being).

children.text: evaṃ sa dānapratipattiśūraḥ karoti kāye 'pi na jātvapekṣām /
children.translated_text: Thus, that hero of the practice of giving (<s>dāna</s>) never has regard even for [his own] body;
his actions of speech, body, and mind attain purity without effort.

children.text: viśuddhakarmā ca hitaṃ pareṣām āyāsaduḥkhena vinā karoti /
children.translated_text: And being of purified action, he accomplishes the benefit of others without the suffering of exertion;

children.text: itthaṃ sa sattvārthamabhiprayatno nayānaye kauśalamabhyupaiti // Ps_1.14 //
children.translated_text: thus, striving for the welfare of beings, he attains skill in right and wrong methods (<s>naya</s> and <s>anaya</s>).

children.text: bhūyastaraṃ prāpya balaṃ sa dānāt saddharmadānena tataḥ karoti /
children.translated_text: Having gained greater strength from giving, he then makes, through the gift of the true <s>Dharma</s>,

children.text: bhavāndhakāre bhramatāṃ janānāṃ sūryodayāt spaṣṭataraṃ prakāśam // Ps_1.15 //
children.translated_text: an illumination clearer than sunrise for people wandering in the darkness of existence (<s>bhava</s>).
The accomplishment of the welfare and benefit of the world, established in the arising of omniscience (<s>sarvajñabhāva</s>) —
therefore his inexhaustible merit arises like the radiance of the sun standing at its rising.
Such are the wondrous floods of virtues born of giving that become the ornaments of <s>bodhisattvas</s> —

children.text: tasmāt tadīyaṃ parikarma cittaṃ dānasya kāruṇyapuraḥsarasya // Ps_1.17 //
children.translated_text: therefore one should prepare the mind for giving, preceded by compassion (<s>kāruṇya</s>).
'By this [giving] may I accomplish for the world the Buddhist [qualities of] longevity, eloquence, strength, and the like;

children.text: sattvā mayā cāmiṣasaṃgṛhītāḥ saddharmapātrāṇyapi me bhaveyuḥ // Ps_1.18 //
children.translated_text: and may the beings attracted by me through material gifts also become vessels of the true <s>Dharma</s>.'
Thus the wise one gives the gift of food — not for the sake of obtaining heavenly fortune,

children.text: pānānyapi kleśatṛṣaḥ śamāya lokasya lokārthacaro dadāti // Ps_1.19 //
children.translated_text: and gives drinks too for the quenching of the thirst of the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) of the world, acting for the world's benefit.
'How may the entire world become a recipient of the Buddhist miraculous powers

children.text: lābhī kathaṃ syāditi lokanātho yānaṃ mahāyānaratirdadāti // Ps_1.20 //
children.translated_text: and the bliss of <s>Nirvāṇa</s>?' — thus thinking, the Protector of the World, who delights in the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, gives vehicles.

children.text: saṃbuddhavarṇasya ca hemabhāso lajjāmayasyaiva ca bhūṣaṇasya /
children.translated_text: For the attainment of the golden luster of a perfect <s>Buddha</s>'s complexion and of the ornament that is modesty,

children.text: niṣpattaye vastravidhīnudārān satkṛtya kālānuguṇaṃ dadāti // Ps_1.21 //
children.translated_text: he respectfully gives generous gifts of clothing at the appropriate time.
Looking toward the seat at the <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s> (place of awakening) [as the purpose for giving] seats and beds — the three kinds of resting-place —

children.text: sarvajñacakṣuḥpratilabdhaye ca caityeṣu rathyāsu ca dīpamālām // Ps_1.22 //
children.translated_text: and for the attainment of the eye of omniscience, [he gives] rows of lamps in <s>caityas</s> (shrines) and in the streets.
Musical instruments for the purpose of gathering [beings through] divine hearing, and gifts of incense for the character of a perfect <s>Buddha</s>;
halls, embankments, parks, <s>vihāras</s> (monasteries), and dwellings — he gives, intent upon being a refuge.
The gift of well-prepared flavors, for the attainment of supremacy in the essence of essences;

children.text: bhaiṣajyadānānyajarāmaratvaṃ lokān imān prāpayituṃ dadāti // Ps_1.24 //
children.translated_text: gifts of medicine he gives to lead these worlds to the state of agelessness and deathlessness.
Wishing to lead to freedom equal to his own the world that has been enslaved by the host of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions),

children.text: sa dāsadāsyādi sadā dadāti dāsānudāsānaparākariṣyan // Ps_1.25 //
children.translated_text: he always gives servants, maidservants, and the like — never degrading the servants and their servants.
He gives sons, daughters, and beloved ones — a blameless gift, because of his love for <s>Bodhi</s> (awakening);
and being devoted exclusively to delight in the true <s>Dharma</s>, [he gives] special pleasures that are causes of delight.
He gives gold, pearls, gems, coral, and the like for the attainment of excellent marks (<s>lakṣaṇas</s>),
and jewel-blazing, variegated ornaments for the beauty of the minor marks (<s>anuvyañjanas</s>).
Gardens and ascetic groves for the purpose of <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), and a treasure of wealth for the treasury of the true <s>Dharma</s>;
unwearied, he gives kingdoms adorned with sovereign authority, for the kingship of the Lord of Sages (<s>Munīndra</s>).
With his excellent feet marked with wheels (<s>cakra</s>), out of eagerness to step upon the seat of <s>Saṃbodhi</s> (complete awakening),
he, unperturbed, gives the gift of [his] feet — the one who accomplishes the welfare of the world.

children.text: duḥkhāpagāyāmatiśīghragāyāṃ magnasya lokasya kathaṃ na dadyām /
children.translated_text: 'For a path that leads to the removal of suffering, extremely swift — how could I not give
hands that are [to become] the hands of the true <s>Dharma</s>?' — thus he bestows hands radiant as freshly-bloomed lotuses.
For the fulfillment of the faculties of faith (<s>śraddhā</s>) and the rest, he gives ears, nose, and the like, unwearied;
and eyes — [eyes] that will purify the vision of the world through the abandonment of all obscurations (<s>āvaraṇas</s>).

children.text: utkṛtya māṃsāni saśoṇitāni dadāti kāruṇyavaśena nāthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having cut out flesh together with blood, the Protector (<s>Nātha</s>) gives [them] through the power of compassion:

children.text: bhūmyagnivāyvambuvadeva me syāllokopajīvyaḥ katham eṣa kāyaḥ // Ps_1.32 //
children.translated_text: 'Like earth, fire, wind, and water — how should this body of mine be [anything other than] that upon which the world subsists?'
For the attainment of the supreme knowledge of the world, he honors [seekers] even with his head (<s>uttamāṅga</s>);
how much more readily [does he fulfill] the request of a needy person who has come, with other bodily parts?

children.text: majjānamapyadbhutavīraceṣṭo dadāti lokasya kathaṃ na kuryām /
children.translated_text: Even marrow he gives — of wondrous heroic deeds: 'How could I not do [this] for the world,

children.text: tathāgataṃ vigrahamapradhṛṣyaṃ vṛṣṭyāpi vajrojjvalayā patantyā // Ps_1.34 //
children.translated_text: [in order to obtain] the invincible body of a <s>Tathāgata</s>, [which cannot be harmed] even by a rain of blazing <s>vajras</s> (thunderbolts) falling [upon it]?'
Thus, this ever-blameless [giving], poured forth by the <s>bodhisattva</s> like a rain-cloud —
having refreshed the entire world with the water of giving, approaches the ocean of omniscience (<s>sarvajñatā</s>).

children.text: anviṣya bhogānviṣameṇa nāsau dadāti notpīḍanayā parasya /
children.translated_text: He does not give having acquired enjoyments by wrongful means, nor by oppressing another,
nor as a cause of fear, shame, or retaliation, nor seeking [only] those worthy of gifts.

children.text: na ca praṇīte sati rūkṣadānam adakṣiṇīyā iti vāvamanya /
children.translated_text: Nor [does he give] a coarse gift when an excellent one is [available], nor [does he] despise [recipients] as unworthy of gifts,

children.text: vipākakāṅkṣākṛpaṇīkṛtaṃ vā satkārahīnaṃ vijugupsitaṃ vā // Ps_1.37 //
children.translated_text: nor [does he give what is] made wretched by craving for karmic results, or lacking in respect, or disgusting.

children.text: naivonnatiṃ śīlavate prayacchan viparyayaṃ gacchati netarasmai /
children.translated_text: When giving eminence to the virtuous, he does not act conversely toward others;

children.text: nātmānamutkarṣati naiva nindāṃ karoti so 'nyasya samaprayogaḥ // Ps_1.38 //
children.translated_text: he does not exalt himself nor reproach another — equal in his treatment [of all].
He has no gift with false intention, nor does he have a gift without intention;

children.text: na krodhadoṣopahataṃ dadāti naivānutāpaṃ kurute sa dattvā // Ps_1.39 //
children.translated_text: he does not give what is marred by the fault of anger, nor does he feel regret after giving.

children.text: na ślāghyamāno vipulaṃ dadāti nāślāghyamāno 'nyataraṃ dadāti /
children.translated_text: He does not give abundantly while boasting, nor does he give a lesser gift while not boasting;

children.text: na yācakānāmupaghātadānaṃ yad vā bhaved vipratipattihetuḥ // Ps_1.40 //
children.translated_text: nor [does he give] a gift that would harm the petitioners, or would be a cause of confusion.

children.text: nākāladānaṃ sa dadāti kiṃcid dadāti kāle viṣame 'pi naiva /
children.translated_text: He never gives a gift at the wrong time, nor gives even at an uneven [inappropriate] time;

children.text: na devabhāvāya na rājyahetorna hīnayānaspṛhayālubhāvāt // Ps_1.41 //
children.translated_text: not for the sake of divine status, not for the sake of sovereignty, not from a longing and craving for the <s>Hīnayāna</s> (Lesser Vehicle).

children.text: nāsau mukhollokanayā dadāti na kīrtiśabdāya na hāsyahetoḥ /
children.translated_text: He does not give while looking at [the recipient's] face, not for the sake of fame, not for the sake of laughter;

children.text: paryāptametacca mameti naivaṃ yadvā vihiṃsāhasitaṃ pareṣām // Ps_1.42 //
children.translated_text: never [thinking] 'This is enough for me,' nor [giving] what involves injury or ridicule of others.

children.text: sarvajñabhāvāpariṇāmitaṃ vā sagarhitaṃ vā sa dadāti naiva /
children.translated_text: He never gives what is not dedicated to the state of omniscience (<s>sarvajñabhāva</s>), nor what is blameworthy;

children.text: tato 'sya tat pāramitābhidhānaṃ parāṃ viśuddhiṃ samupaiti dānam // Ps_1.43 //
children.translated_text: therefore his giving, bearing the name of a perfection (<s>pāramitā</s>), attains the highest purity.

children.text: dānodbhavaṃ tasya ca puṇyarāśiṃ lokāt samagrādapi piṇḍitāni /
children.translated_text: The mass of merit born from his giving — even all the merits gathered from the entire world

children.text: puṇyāni naivābhibhavanti yasmāllokottamattvaṃ sa tato 'bhyupaiti // Ps_1.44 //
children.translated_text: cannot surpass it; therefore he attains the supreme status in the world.
Established in the five <s>abhijñās</s> (superknowledges), when he rains the rain of giving upon the world —

children.text: samantatastasya kutaḥ pramāṇaṃ parikṣayo vā satatapravṛtteḥ // Ps_1.45 //
children.translated_text: How could there be a measure of that from all sides, or an exhaustion of what is constantly active? (Ps 1.45cd)

children.text: yadakṣayāṇāṃ jagatāṃ hitāya jñānasya hetuśca yadakṣayasya /
children.translated_text: That which is for the benefit of imperishable beings, and which is the cause of imperishable knowledge,

children.text: traidhātukena kṣayiṇā na tacca saṃlipyate vyomavadambudena // Ps_1.46 //
children.translated_text: is not stained by the perishable triple realm, just as the sky is not [stained] by clouds. (Ps 1.46)
That which is concentrated in the aspect of <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness), and free from the faults of signs (<s>nimitta</s>),
accomplished through separation from defilements of possessiveness — therefore it is declared imperishable by the lords of sages. (Ps 1.47)

children.text: asmin punaḥ satpuruṣāvadāne dāne nidāne sukhavistārāṇām /
children.translated_text: In this noble narrative, concerning giving (<s>dāna</s>) which is the source of the expansion of happiness,

children.text: cikīrṣatā yogamanityasaṃjñā bhogeṣu kāryā karuṇā ca loke // Ps_1.48 //
children.translated_text: one who wishes to practice should cultivate the perception of impermanence regarding enjoyments, and compassion toward the world. (Ps 1.48)

children.text: bhogānanityānabhivīkṣamānaḥ sātmyaṃ gatāyāṃ ca tataḥ kṛpāyām /
children.translated_text: Seeing enjoyments as impermanent, and when compassion has become natural,

children.text: sa niścayaṃ gacchati dīyate yad etān madīyāṃ na tu yadgṛhe me // Ps_1.49 //
children.translated_text: he arrives at the conviction: 'What is given is truly mine; not what is in my house.' (Ps 1.49)

children.text: yaddattam asmān na bhayaṃ kadā cid gehe yadasmādbhayamabhyupaiti /
children.translated_text: From what is given, fear never arises; from what is in the house, fear approaches.

children.text: sādhāraṇaṃ rakṣyamatarpakaṃ ca datte tu naite prabhavantyanarthāḥ // Ps_1.50 //
children.translated_text: [Wealth in the house] is common [to thieves], must be guarded, and is unsatisfying; but in what is given, these misfortunes do not arise. (Ps 1.50)

children.text: sukhaṃ paratrāpi karoti dattam ihaiva duḥkhaṃ prakarotyadattam /
children.translated_text: What is given brings happiness even in the next world; what is not given causes suffering in this very life.

children.text: ulkāsvabhāvaṃ hi dhanaṃ narāṇām atyajyamānaṃ vyasanaṃ dadāti // Ps_1.51 //
children.translated_text: For the wealth of men is like a firebrand by nature — when not relinquished, it gives misfortune. (Ps 1.51)

children.text: adīyamānaṃ nidhanaṃ prayāti nidhānatāṃ yāti hi dīyamānam /
children.translated_text: When not given, [wealth] goes to destruction; when given, it becomes a treasure indeed.

children.text: dhanasya niḥsāralaghoḥ sa sāro yaddīyate lokahitonmukhena // Ps_1.52 //
children.translated_text: The essence of wealth, which is insubstantial and light, is what is given by one devoted to the world's welfare. (Ps 1.52)
What is given — this is praiseworthy among the wise; the foolish person praises its accumulation.

children.text: prāyo viyogo hi parigrahebhyo dānādbhavatyabhyudayo yaśaśca // Ps_1.53 //
children.translated_text: For separation from possessions is mostly [inevitable]; from giving arise prosperity and fame. (Ps 1.53)
What is given does not lead to the seizing of defilements; stinginess (<s>mātsarya</s>) is the ignoble quality that leads to suffering.

children.text: yaddīyate satpatha eṣa tasmād ato 'nyathā kāpathamāhurāryāḥ // Ps_1.54 //
children.translated_text: What is given is therefore the true path; otherwise, the noble ones call it a wrong path. (Ps 1.54)
When a supplicant has arrived — since he is the cause for the growth of the equipment for perfect awakening (<s>saṃbodhi-saṃbhāra</s>),

children.text: tatpreṣyasaṃjñātmani saṃniveśyā kalyāṇamitrapriyatā ca tasmin // Ps_1.55 //
children.translated_text: one should place in oneself the notion of being his servant, and [cultivate] fondness for him as a spiritual friend (<s>kalyāṇamitra</s>). (Ps 1.55)
Since for great souls, passions and the like become thin upon hearing of a supplicant,
thereby, surpassing even the arrival of a festival, the approach of a supplicant is dear to them. (Ps 1.56)

children.text: sa cetpunaryācanake 'pi labdhe dātuṃ na śaknotyatidurbalatvāt /
children.translated_text: But if, even when a supplicant is obtained, one is unable to give due to extreme poverty,

children.text: tenānuneyo madhureṇa sāmnā sa yācakaḥ syānna yathā samanyuḥ // Ps_1.57 //
children.translated_text: then that supplicant should be consoled with sweet words, so that he may not become angry. (Ps 1.57)

children.text: kāryaśca mātsaryavinigrahāya mohaprahāṇāya ca tena yatnaḥ /
children.translated_text: And one should make effort to restrain stinginess (<s>mātsarya</s>) and to abandon delusion (<s>moha</s>),

children.text: tathā yathā yācanakaḥ kadā cid vaimukhyadīno na tato vyāpaiti // Ps_1.58 //
children.translated_text: so that a supplicant may never depart from him dejected by refusal. (Ps 1.58)

children.text: saṃbodhicittaṃ kuta eva tasya dravye 'pi yo matsaramabhyupaiti /
children.translated_text: How can there be the mind of awakening (<s>bodhicitta</s>) in one who harbors stinginess even toward material things?

children.text: vāsaḥ sucittasya hi nāsti doṣairambhonidhānasya śavairyathaiva // Ps_1.59 //
children.translated_text: For faults have no dwelling in a pure mind, just as corpses [have no dwelling] in the ocean. (Ps 1.59)

children.text: tasmāt tyaktvā sarvataḥ sarvadoṣān bodhiprārthī sarvadā sarvadaḥ syāt /
children.translated_text: Therefore, having abandoned all faults in every way, one aspiring to awakening (<s>bodhi</s>) should always be a giver of everything.

children.text: trātuṃ lokānekavīraḥ kva cittaṃ ceṣṭā dainyānūrjiteyaṃ kva caiva // Ps_1.60 //
children.translated_text: Where is the mind [that aspires] to save the world as a lone hero, and where is this enfeebled action of poverty? (Ps 1.60)

children.text: mūlaṃ dānasyāsya saṃbodhicittaṃ tanna tyājyaṃ ditsatā dānamīdṛk /
children.translated_text: The root of this giving is the mind of awakening (<s>bodhicitta</s>); one who wishes to give such a gift should not abandon it.
The fully awakened ones (<s>Saṃbuddhas</s>) declare him the foremost among the generous — he who desires to practice the foremost renunciation in the worlds. (Ps 1.61)
[Colophon:] The Summary of the Perfection of Giving (<s>Dāna-pāramitā-samāsa</s>).
2. The Summary of the Perfection of Morality (<s>Śīla-pāramitā-samāsa</s>).
In order to make people beautiful with the ornament of the morality of the fully awakened (<s>Saṃbuddha</s>), with zeal that has arisen,

children.text: svameva śīlaṃ pariśodhyamādau śīlaṃ hi śakterbalamādadhāti // Ps_2.1 //
children.translated_text: one should first purify one's own morality (<s>śīla</s>); for morality bestows the strength of power. (Ps 2.1)

children.text: loke tathā prema niveśayeta svapne 'pi na droharuciryathā syāt /
children.translated_text: One should so establish love in the world that even in a dream one would not delight in harm;

children.text: paropakāraikarasaḥ pareṣāṃ bhogānahīnāmiva na spṛśecca // Ps_2.2 //
children.translated_text: devoted solely to helping others, one should not touch the possessions of others, as if they were lowly. (Ps 2.2)
With a mind turned away from the course of duality, all the more from attachment to another's wife,

children.text: kurvīta lokasya hitārthakartā kāyena ceṣṭāḥ sujanasya ceṣṭāḥ // Ps_2.3 //
children.translated_text: one who acts for the world's benefit should perform with the body the actions of a good person. (Ps 2.3)
Speech that is charming with sweetness, timely, in accordance with truth, and non-divisive —
one should speak words aimed at the attainment of the truth of the true <s>Dharma</s>, having ceased from their opposite. (Ps 2.4)

children.text: kāryaṃ prayatnena mayā yadasmai tatsādhanena svayameva labdham /
children.translated_text: 'What must be accomplished with effort by me for this person — that has been obtained by the very means itself' —

children.text: parasya saukhyeṣviti tuṣṭacittaḥ kuryān manonirviṣayāmabhidhyām // Ps_2.5 //
children.translated_text: thus content-minded regarding others' happiness, one should make covetousness (<s>abhidhyā</s>) objectless. (Ps 2.5)

children.text: mamaiva daurabalyamidaṃ yadeṣa kleśāsvatantraḥ svahitaṃ na vetti /
children.translated_text: 'This is indeed my weakness, that this person, under the power of defilements (<s>kleśa</s>), does not know his own good' —

children.text: parāparādheṣvapi kārya evaṃ vyāpādavahnipraśamāya yatnaḥ // Ps_2.6 //
children.translated_text: even concerning others' offenses, effort should thus be made to quench the fire of malice (<s>vyāpāda</s>). (Ps 2.6)
And having expelled with the lights of knowledge the spreading darkness called wrong views (<s>kudṛṣṭi</s>) from the mind,
one should cultivate unshakeable devotion toward the best of gods and men (<s>Naradeva-varya</s>, i.e. the <s>Buddha</s>), rooted in the practice of virtues. (Ps 2.7)

children.text: svargasya mokṣasya ca satpathebhyo naivoccalet karmapathebhya ebhyaḥ /
children.translated_text: One should never deviate from these paths of action (<s>karmapatha</s>), which are the true paths to heaven and liberation;

children.text: atra sthitānāṃ hi jagaddhitārthāścintāviśeṣāḥ saphalībhavanti // Ps_2.8 //
children.translated_text: for those established herein, the special contemplations for the world's benefit bear fruit. (Ps 2.8)

children.text: samāsataḥ śīlamidaṃ vadanti yaḥ saṃvaraḥ kāyavacomanastaḥ /
children.translated_text: In summary, they call this morality: the restraint (<s>saṃvara</s>) of body, speech, and mind;

children.text: kārtsnyena cātraiva yataḥ sa tasmād etānyayatnena viśodhayecca // Ps_2.9 //
children.translated_text: since the whole [of morality] is right here, therefore one should purify these effortlessly. (Ps 2.9)
One whose love is turned away from violence gives fearlessness (<s>abhaya</s>) to people by his gentle nature,

children.text: yā vāsanā doṣakṛtāsya citte tāṃ cāprayatnena samucchinatti // Ps_2.10 //
children.translated_text: and the impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>) created by faults in his mind — these too he eradicates without effort. (Ps 2.10)

children.text: maitrīviśeṣānugate ca citte vairānubandheṣu śamam gateṣu /
children.translated_text: And when the mind follows special loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>), when the chains of enmity have come to peace,
he awakens happily and sleeps happily, with the faults of disturbing inauspicious dreams vanished. (Ps 2.11)

children.text: kurvanti rakṣāṃsyapi cāsya rakṣāṃ na durgatibhyo bhayamabhyupaiti /
children.translated_text: Even <s>Rākṣasas</s> (demons) provide him protection; fear of bad rebirths does not approach him.
And he attains a long life adorned with the quality of health, established in happy rebirth (<s>sugati</s>). (Ps 2.12)
And therefore, of the <s>Tathāgatas</s> who have attained perfect awakening (<s>saṃbodhi</s>), the immeasurable extent [is such that]

children.text: nirvartate cittavaśānuvarti lokasya saukhyopacayāya vāyuḥ // Ps_2.13 //
children.translated_text: the wind arises, following the command of their minds, for the increase of the world's happiness. (Ps 2.13)

children.text: anādadānastu parasya bhogān āpnoti bhogānmahataḥ paratra /
children.translated_text: One who does not take others' possessions attains great enjoyments in the next world,
unshakeable even by hosts of royal heirs, like mountains unshakeable by wind. (Ps 2.14)
One attains dearness that follows purity of conduct, and trustworthiness, in this very life;
therefore, free from fear of others' attacks, one never encounters obstruction of [one's] path. (Ps 2.15)
One of pure morality effortlessly develops the understanding that expanses of wealth are without essence;
therefore, with a mind purified of secondary defilements (<s>upakleśa</s>), one spontaneously reaches unsurpassed awakening (<s>bodhi</s>). (Ps 2.16)
Having ceased from wrong conduct regarding sensual pleasures, beautiful with tranquility through mastery of the senses,

children.text: prāpnoti lokastutibhiḥ samantāt kīrtiṃ diganteṣu vikīryamāṇam // Ps_2.17 //
children.translated_text: one attains fame praised by the world on all sides, scattered to the ends of the directions. (Ps 2.17)

children.text: na cāpi kaṃ citpramadāsu rāgaṃ karoti mātṛriva vīkṣamāṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: Nor does one develop any passion toward women, regarding them as mothers;

children.text: asmācca puṇyopacayān munīndraḥ saṃjāyate vāraṇavastikoṣaḥ // Ps_2.18 //
children.translated_text: and from this accumulation of merit, the lord of sages is born with a sheathed member like an elephant's. (Ps 2.18)
Turning away from false speech, with a mind freed from delight in deceit and desire for fraud,

children.text: ādeyasiddhyā vacanasya sattvān karoti dharmābhimukhān ayatnāt // Ps_2.19 //
children.translated_text: through the effectiveness of his trustworthy words, he effortlessly turns beings toward the <s>Dharma</s>. (Ps 2.19)

children.text: divaukasāṃ ca priyatāṃ yadeti satyapriyaścitramidaṃ na tādṛk /
children.translated_text: That one who loves truth attains dearness even among the gods — this is no great wonder;

children.text: devasvabhāvo guṇapakṣapātī pratyakṣiṇastaccariteṣu te ca // Ps_2.20 //
children.translated_text: for the nature of gods is to favor virtue, and they directly witness such conduct. (Ps 2.20)
That he becomes an authority and beloved of worldly people — this is the wonder here;

children.text: prāyeṇa loko hi guṇairdaridraḥ svenānumānena parānminoti // Ps_2.21 //
children.translated_text: for the world, generally poor in virtues, evaluates others by its own measure. (Ps 2.21)
As if abandoning groves of blue lotuses, one who discerns distinction [turns] toward the blooming lotus;
in his face there takes refuge the delightful fragrance-arrangement that brings joy. (Ps 2.22)
Seeing things equal and unequal with radiant knowledge that delivers from bad rebirths,

children.text: sa ātmasākṣī samupaiti lajjāṃ yādṛcchikairapyaśubhairvitarkaiḥ // Ps_2.23 //
children.translated_text: he, being his own witness, feels shame even at involuntary unwholesome thoughts. (Ps 2.23)

children.text: evaṃ sa śuddhaprakṛtiḥ krameṇa na śaṅkyate 'nyairna ca śaṅkate 'nyān /
children.translated_text: Thus, being of pure nature gradually, he is not suspected by others nor does he suspect others;

children.text: tato 'sya satyābhyanuvartanī vāgarakṣatāṃ yāti tathāgatatve // Ps_2.24 //
children.translated_text: therefore his speech, which follows truth, attains the state of being unguarded in <s>Tathāgata</s>hood. (Ps 2.24)
The body becomes invulnerable to others' attacks; the wealth of retinue becomes unassailable by others.

children.text: paiśūnyamuktasya bhavatyabhedyā śraddhā ca dharme pratipattisārā // Ps_2.25 //
children.translated_text: For one freed from slander (<s>paiśūnya</s>), faith in the <s>Dharma</s>, whose essence is practice, becomes unbreakable. (Ps 2.25)
He attains indestructible, unfailing loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>), and compassion (<s>kṛpā</s>) that does not abandon the world's purpose;

children.text: prāpnoti cābhedyatamān munitve janmāntarasthānapi śiṣyasaṃghān // Ps_2.26 //
children.translated_text: and in his sagehood he attains the most unbreakable assemblies of disciples, even those from other lifetimes. (Ps 2.26)
The spreading dust-cloud of anger's vanguard army, scattered by the fierce wind of [wrong] intention,
which destroys the body of fame — harsh speech (<s>paruṣābhidhāna</s>) should be removed by the rain-clouds of loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>). (Ps 2.27)
Turned away from this [harsh speech], with sweet words one brings the minds of the world under one's influence;

children.text: lokasya ca premṇi virūḍhamūle saivāsya vāggrāhyataratvameti // Ps_2.28 //
children.translated_text: And when love for the world has deep-rooted foundations, his speech attains even greater acceptability. // Ps_2.28 //

children.text: ataśca lokāñchataśo vinīya teṣāṃ samāvṛtya ca duḥkhamārgam /
children.translated_text: And thus, having guided the people in hundreds,and having blocked their path of suffering,

children.text: na durgatiṃ gacchati puṇyakarmā dharmo hi rakṣeha paratra caiva // Ps_2.29 //
children.translated_text: the meritorious one does not go to a bad destination, for <s>dharma</s> (righteousness) protects here and in the hereafter. // Ps_2.29 //
With clearly resounding footsteps even from afar, glorious; with a nature of happiness even nearby,
more exalted than the sound of a thundercloud — his <s>Brahma</s>-voice adorns his mouth. // Ps_2.30 //
Having ceased from false speech, he attains the exclusive affection of the discerning;

children.text: satyābhidhāne kramate sabuddhiḥ prāpnoti māhātmyam akṛtrimaṃ ca // Ps_2.31 //
children.translated_text: the intelligent one advances in truthful utterance and attains unfeigned greatness. // Ps_2.31 //
And from this merit, in the state of the King of Sages (<s>Munirāja</s>), being questioned

children.text: praśnānanekānapi caikakāle niḥsaṃśayaṃ vyākurute sa vācā // Ps_2.32 //
children.translated_text: about numerous questions even at a single time, he answers with his voice without any doubt. // Ps_2.32 //
Having wisely abandoned covetousness — which bears fruitless results both here and hereafter —

children.text: anīrṣyabhāvādatikāṅkṣitāṃ sa prāpnoti vistīrṇatarāṃ samṛddhim // Ps_2.33 //
children.translated_text: through freedom from envy, he attains the most widely desired and expansive prosperity. // Ps_2.33 //

children.text: citte viśuddhe ca tadāśrayāṇi vākkāyakarmāṇi śucībhavanti /
children.translated_text: And when the mind is purified, the actions of speech and body that depend on it become pure,
like the circles of the constellations in the sky adorned by the qualities of time. // Ps_2.34 //
And from the sovereignty of merit, his intellect advances toward ever-excellent enjoyments,

children.text: prayāti rājñāmapi saṃmatatvam adhṛṣyatāṃ ca pratigarvitānām // Ps_2.35 //
children.translated_text: and he attains the esteem even of kings and the invincibility of the proud. // Ps_2.35 //
His sense faculties, empowered by righteous deeds, do not suffer deficiency,

children.text: ataśca lokatrayapūjya ekaḥ śāstā bhavatyaprativartyacakraḥ // Ps_2.36 //
children.translated_text: and therefore, as the one Teacher worshipped by the three worlds, he becomes the one whose wheel cannot be turned back. // Ps_2.36 //
Freed from the fever and burning of ill-will, with a nature inclined to goodness, acting with wisdom,
he manifests, as it were, the serenity of mind through his calm and peaceful conduct. // Ps_2.37 //

children.text: hiṃsātmake vigrahasaṃhite vā karmaṇyanāryācarite śaṭhe vā /
children.translated_text: In violent action attended by conflict, in ignoble and deceitful conduct,

children.text: na cāsya buddhiḥ kramate kadācin maitrīsukhāsvādaviśeṣalābhāt // Ps_2.38 //
children.translated_text: his mind never inclines, because he has gained the special taste of the joy of <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness). // Ps_2.38 //
In the world he attains equality with noble people and is honored by people as if a deity;

children.text: na brahmaloko 'pi ca durlabho 'sya prasnigdhakarmaṇyamanaḥpathasya // Ps_2.39 //
children.translated_text: even the <s>Brahma</s>-world is not difficult to attain for one whose mind's path is devoted to compassionate action. // Ps_2.39 //
Rejoicing in the welfare of beings, he effortlessly brings peace to their minds,

children.text: ramyaḥ śaratkāla ivāpagānāṃ toyāni meghāgamadūṣitāni // Ps_2.40 //
children.translated_text: delightful like the autumn season [that purifies] the waters of rivers polluted by the arrival of clouds. // Ps_2.40 //
With a form pleasing to all, a seat of knowledge, with wondrous conduct,

children.text: ekīkarotīva tato munitve lokasya vijñānapṛthaktvasiddhim // Ps_2.41 //
children.translated_text: he unifies, as it were, the diversity of the world's understanding in sagehood. // Ps_2.41 //
Treading through the mire of wrong views, he gains companions of virtuous heart,

children.text: karmasvako 'stīti ca karma pāpaṃ viśasyamāno 'pi karoti naiva // Ps_2.42 //
children.translated_text: and knowing 'one reaps one's own <s>karma</s> (actions),' even when urged, he never commits sinful deeds. // Ps_2.42 //
His devotion to the <s>Jina</s> (the Victorious One, Buddha) becomes unshakable, and he is not led astray by curiosities and auspicious signs;

children.text: ārye ca mārge labhate pratiṣṭhāṃ viśeṣagāmitvamato 'bhyupaiti // Ps_2.43 //
children.translated_text: he gains establishment on the Noble Path and thereby attains the state of going to distinction. // Ps_2.43 //

children.text: satkāyadṛṣṭyuccalitaḥ sa yāti na durgatiṃ hetuparikṣayeṇa /
children.translated_text: Freed from the view of the existing body (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>), he does not go to a bad destination, through the exhaustion of causes;
and endowed with unobstructed knowledge, he wanders unattached between heaven and earth. // Ps_2.44 //
And those qualities unattained even by <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> (solitary awakened ones) all become manifest for him,
the qualities of the Lord of Sages expanding for the welfare of the world, leading to the state of omniscience (<s>sarvajñabhāva</s>). // Ps_2.45 //
This magnificence, variegated with jewels of virtues, praiseworthy, delightful with self-evident qualities —

children.text: ko nāma vidvān na samādadīta viśeṣataḥ sattvahitābhilāṣī // Ps_2.46 //
children.translated_text: what wise person, especially one desiring the welfare of beings, would not embrace it? // Ps_2.46 //

children.text: divyābhirāmā manujeṣu saṃpat prakṛṣṭasaukhyaikarasā ca divyā /
children.translated_text: A divine and delightful prosperity among humans, and a divine [prosperity] whose sole essence is supreme happiness —

children.text: śīlādyadi syāt kimivātra citraṃ yasmāt prarohantyapi buddhadharmāḥ // Ps_2.47 //
children.translated_text: if it comes from <s>śīla</s> (moral conduct) and the rest, what wonder is there in this, since even the qualities of a <s>Buddha</s> spring from it? // Ps_2.47 //
One who has fallen from <s>śīla</s> (moral conduct) is incapable even of his own welfare — in what service for another's benefit is he competent?
Therefore, especially for one who accomplishes the welfare of others, laxity in regard to this is not proper. // Ps_2.48 //
Therefore, seeing the intense danger, one should avoid even the slightest thing to be avoided;

children.text: na bodhisattvābhyucitaṃ ca śīlaṃ vikhaṇḍayedātmasukhodayena // Ps_2.49 //
children.translated_text: one should not violate the <s>śīla</s> (moral conduct) befitting a <s>Bodhisattva</s> for the sake of one's own pleasure. // Ps_2.49 //
Nor should one make one's <s>śīla</s> riddled with faults of weakness — by gazing at women, dalliance, massages, and the like;

children.text: na durjanakleśaparigrahād vā kurvīta śīlaṃ śabalaprakāram // Ps_2.50 //
children.translated_text: nor should one make one's <s>śīla</s> spotted by embracing the afflictions of wicked people. // Ps_2.50 //
One should cultivate <s>śīla</s> (moral conduct) that is free from the stains of impurity, augmented exclusively by pure [deeds],
going freely by its own will, blameless, adorned by the praise of the wise. // Ps_2.51 //
And through fulfilling all the rules of training, it is complete, free from impatience,
with intense practices devoted solely to the welfare of others, reflecting the purity of the mind. // Ps_2.52 //
Relying on mindfulness, one should be devoted to the protection of <s>śīla</s> (moral conduct) through restraint of the senses,
as if about to dispel with a thousand rays the great darkness of the world's immorality. // Ps_2.53 //
With ointments, bandages, and the like for bodily wounds, which serve as remedies for suffering,
obtained through proper means, one should be content in mind and not anxious about looking at others. // Ps_2.54 //
Even while engaged in all praiseworthy virtues conducive to <s>śīla</s>,
one should not be proud, due to the absence of self-amazement, and should fear the fame that arises from it. // Ps_2.55 //
For the mode of gain, arising from the display of virtues, approaches enmity wearing the face of friendship,

children.text: saroruhāṇāmiva śītaraśmiḥ śreyaḥ pramāthī śithilavratānām // Ps_2.56 //
children.translated_text: like the cold-rayed moon [that harms] lotuses — destructive of the good for those of lax vows. // Ps_2.56 //

children.text: śīlaṃ guṇābhyāsavidhiṃ vadanti saṃbodhicitte ca guṇāḥ samagrāḥ /
children.translated_text: They call <s>śīla</s> (moral conduct) the method of practicing virtues, and in <s>bodhicitta</s> (the mind of awakening) all virtues are complete;

children.text: abhyasyate tacca kṛpāguṇena kāruṇyaśīlaḥ satataṃ tataḥ syāt // Ps_2.57 //
children.translated_text: that is practiced through the quality of compassion, and therefore one should always be of compassionate nature. // Ps_2.57 //

children.text: yanniśritaṃ kāmabhave 'pi naiva saṃtiṣṭhate naiva ca rūpadhātau /
children.translated_text: That which, when relied upon, does not abide even in the realm of desire, nor in the form-realm,

children.text: ārūpyadhātau yadasaṃsthitaṃ ca tattattvataḥ śīlamudāharanti // Ps_2.58 //
children.translated_text: and which is unestablished in the formless realm — that they call <s>śīla</s> in its true nature. // Ps_2.58 //
He who wishes to establish all beings in <s>śīla</s> in immeasurable world-systems,

children.text: niṣevate lokahitāya śīlaṃ taducyate pāramiteti tajjñaiḥ // Ps_2.59 //
children.translated_text: and practices <s>śīla</s> for the welfare of the world — that is called <s>pāramitā</s> (perfection) by the knowers. // Ps_2.59 //
<s>Śīla</s> (moral conduct) is the path to special attainment, the heritage of those of compassionate nature,
of pure nature for the excellence of knowledge, the foremost ornament-type with no arising of destruction. // Ps_2.60 //
A fragrant ointment whose pleasing scent pervades the three worlds, not opposed to the renunciant life;

children.text: tulyākṛtibhyo 'pi pṛthagjanebhyaḥ śīlaṃ viśeṣaṃ kurute narāṇām // Ps_2.61 //
children.translated_text: <s>śīla</s> (moral conduct) distinguishes people even from those of similar appearance among ordinary folk. // Ps_2.61 //
Even without boasting, through steadfast character, without the exertion of varied speech,
[there arises] a sovereignty before which all the world bows, free from pride and arrogance. // Ps_2.62 //
Even of those without distinguished lineage, even of those who do not perform the essence of service,

children.text: niṣkevale śīlavidhau sthitānām asaṃstutānāmapi yannarāṇām // Ps_2.63 //
children.translated_text: of those men who are established in the pure practice of <s>śīla</s> alone, even those who are not acclaimed —
the dust from their feet, purified [by their touch], obtained through bowing,

children.text: cūḍāgralagnāni manuṣyadevāḥ śrīmattaraṃ śīlamataḥ kulebhyaḥ // Ps_2.64 //
children.translated_text: is borne upon the crowns of human and divine beings — therefore <s>śīla</s> is more glorious than [noble] families. // Ps_2.64 //

children.text: tasmān na durgatibhayena na rājyahetorna svargasaṃpadabhilāṣasamudbhavena /
children.translated_text: Therefore, one should not practice pure <s>śīla</s> out of fear of bad destinations, nor for the sake of kingship,

children.text: seveta śīlamamalaṃ na hi tattathā syāllokārthasiddhiparamastu bhajeta śīlam // Ps_2.65 //
children.translated_text: nor from desire born of longing for heavenly prosperity — for it would not be so [effective]; one should embrace <s>śīla</s> with supreme dedication to accomplishing the welfare of the world. // Ps_2.65 //
// [Thus ends] the Summary of the Perfection of Moral Conduct (<s>Śīla-pāramitā-samāsa</s>) //
3. Summary of the Perfection of Patience (<s>Kṣānti-pāramitā-samāsa</s>)

children.text: saṃmohanīṃ manmathapakṣamāyāṃ prāhuḥ sukhāṃ caiva vimokṣamāyām /
children.translated_text: They call the illusion of <s>Manmatha</s> (the god of love), [which belongs to] the side of delusion, pleasant; and the illusion of liberation [pleasant too];

children.text: tasyāṃ na kuryāt kaiva kṣamāyāṃ prayatnamekāntahitakṣamāyām // Ps_3.1 //
children.translated_text: who would not make effort in that patience (<s>kṣamā</s>) which is exclusively beneficial and capable? // Ps_3.1 //
The disposition of the virtuous, always unaware of others' offenses, is delightful;
known by the beautiful name produced by virtue, <s>kṣamā</s> (patience) conducts itself for the welfare of the world, guided by compassion. // Ps_3.2 //
For those whose minds are devoted to the welfare of others, they call forbearance (<s>titikṣā</s>) the first vow;

children.text: seturjalānīva hi roṣadoṣaḥ śreyāṃsi lokasya samāvṛṇoti // Ps_3.3 //
children.translated_text: for the fault of anger, like a dam [blocking] waters, obstructs the good of the world. // Ps_3.3 //
The ornament of those endowed with power, the foremost strength of those rich in <s>tapas</s> (austerity),
a stream of water against the forest fire of ill-will — <s>kṣānti</s> (patience) is the quenching of misfortune here and hereafter. // Ps_3.4 //
On the armor of patience worn by the good, the arrow-words of the wicked are blunted,
and mostly turning into flowers of praise, they become garlands of fame for them. // Ps_3.5 //
The antidote to the poison of wicked speech, shining like the moonlight of knowledge,
the steadfast nature of ascetics — <s>kṣānti</s> (patience) is the ground for the dwelling of virtues. // Ps_3.6 //
The essence of one whose depth is profound, the arrival of clouds to quench the summer heat of anger,

children.text: vyatītavelasya guṇārṇavasya vyāpī svanaḥ kṣāntimayo 'bhyudeti // Ps_3.7 //
children.translated_text: The pervading sound, made of patience, rises from the ocean of virtues whose bounds have been surpassed. // 3.7 //
A stairway ascending up to the <s>Brahma</s>-world, whose defects of weariness have departed,
a workshop for the form that bears the burden of virtues, adorned with the true marks. // 3.8 //
[Patience is] the uprooting of the great trees of faults laden with the fruits of enmity,
a river ever favorable to the ocean of virtues of the developed <s>bodhicitta</s> (awakening mind). // 3.9 //

children.text: śubhā paratrāpi hite samṛddhirjagaddhitārthasya parā vivṛddhiḥ /
children.translated_text: An auspicious prosperity in welfare even in the next world; the supreme growth for one whose purpose is the welfare of the world;
the well-known excellence of an inherently virtuous nature — patience is the purity of mind, body, and speech. // 3.10 //
He is not broken by the faults of <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence), gazing upon beings with compassion-moistened [eyes];

children.text: satkarmabhirlokahitaiḥ samantād yaśomayatvaṃ vrajatīva loke // Ps_3.11 //
children.translated_text: through meritorious deeds beneficial to the world, he seems to attain a state made entirely of fame in the world. // 3.11 //
The patient one is not touched by the faults deemed worthy of astonishment, through the excellence of his knowledge;
and from the arising of the strength of patience regarding impermanence, he never attains excessive joy even in happiness. // 3.12 //
He does not shrink from disgrace, through the spreading power of patience;

children.text: ataśca śeṣairapi lokadharmairaniśritatvānna sa cāpalīti // Ps_3.13 //
children.translated_text: and therefore, since he is unattached even to the remaining worldly conditions (<s>lokadharmāḥ</s>), he does not become fickle. // 3.13 //

children.text: tīvraprakārairapi viprakārairna vikriyāṃ yānti satāṃ manāṃsi /
children.translated_text: The minds of the virtuous are not agitated even by the most severe provocations,
firmly resolved on the state of the chief of sages (<s>Munīndra</s>), well-fashioned by the empowerment of patience. // 3.14 //

children.text: sa kṣāntidhīreṇa ca mānasena kaṣṭāni saṃdarśayate tapāṃsi /
children.translated_text: With a mind made steadfast by patience, he demonstrates difficult austerities,

children.text: darponnatiṃ tīrthakṛtāṃ manaḥsu nīcaiḥ kariṣyan hitakāmyayaiva // Ps_3.15 //
children.translated_text: in order to bring low the pride and arrogance in the minds of the <s>tīrthikas</s> (non-Buddhist teachers), solely out of desire for their benefit. // 3.15 //
This world, deluded by attachment to the self, regarding all others as adversaries,
its mind overcome by the provocations of that [self-grasping], reaches distress from separation from patience. // 3.16 //
The minds of the virtuous, accompanied by compassion, whose ceremonies of well-being have been performed through patience,

children.text: naṣṭātmadṛṣṭiṇi parāpakārān na vikriyāṃ yānti guṇānurāgāt // Ps_3.17 //
children.translated_text: having destroyed the view of self — they are not agitated by the offenses of others, due to their love of virtue. // 3.17 //
A false conceptualization is the cause of anger — a fever of the heart — for those weak in steadfastness;

children.text: samyagvikalpastu samādadhāti kṣāntiprakārāṃ manasaḥ praśāntim // Ps_3.18 //
children.translated_text: but right conceptualization establishes a peace of mind that has the character of patience. // 3.18 //
In the patience that is grounded upon conceptual analysis, there would be no room for wavering,
like the image of the full moon on water stirred by the dawn breeze. // 3.19 //
But in the ultimate sense, the wise who know the truth of patience call the cessation of conceptualization 'patience';
therefore one should strive for the cessation of conceptualization, viewing the world as like a dream. // 3.20 //

children.text: cakṣuḥ kim ākrośati cakṣuretacchrotrādi vākrośati kiṃ tadādi /
children.translated_text: Does the eye revile? Does this eye, the ear, and so forth, revile? What is that?

children.text: yaivaṃ kṣamā sāyatanānvavekṣā na kṣāntireṣā paramārthatastu // Ps_3.21 //
children.translated_text: Such patience, which involves examination of the sense-bases (<s>āyatanas</s>), is not patience in the ultimate sense. // 3.21 //

children.text: vaktā vacaścaitadanityameva śrutirvikalpo 'pi ca yo mamāyam /
children.translated_text: The speaker and this speech are indeed impermanent, as is the hearing, and whatever this conceptualization of 'mine' is —

children.text: anityabhāvapravikalpanaiṣā na kṣāntimetām paramāṃ vadanti // Ps_3.22 //
children.translated_text: this is conceptualizing [things] as impermanent in nature; they do not call this the supreme patience. // 3.22 //

children.text: kartāpakārasya na kaścidasti naivāsti kaścitkriyāte ca yasya /
children.translated_text: There is no agent of the offense, nor is there anyone to whom [the offense] is done;
this is the attainment of the insight of selflessness (<s>nairātmya</s>) — yet this too is not the supreme patience. // 3.23 //
Depending on this and that, phenomena arise — those called blame, praise, pleasure, and pain;
this is the entry-point of dependent origination (<s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>) — this is not the patience that is supremely concentrated. // 3.24 //
If, seized by the great snare of delusion, one's mind is overthrown — 'Surely I am not thus!' —

children.text: ityunnate cāvanate ca citte kṣāntiprakarṣasya kuto 'vakāśaḥ // Ps_3.25 //
children.translated_text: when the mind is exalted and when depressed, how can there be scope for the excellence of patience? // 3.25 //
[Speech,] which perishes, echoing syllable by syllable like an instrument, uttering one by one —

children.text: kuryāṃ kathaṃ kasya ca kāṃ ca pīḍām eṣāpi na kṣāntiratiprakṛṣṭā // Ps_3.26 //
children.translated_text: how and of whom could it cause what pain? This too is not the most excellent patience. // 3.26 //

children.text: yadyesā matpāpaparikṣayārthaṃ na vīkṣate svāmapi dharmapīḍām /
children.translated_text: If, for the sake of exhausting my evil <s>karma</s>, [the provocateur] does not consider even the injury to his own <s>dharma</s> —

children.text: asmān na kalyāṇataraṃ hi mitram asāvapi kṣāntyupacārā eva // Ps_3.27 //
children.translated_text: there is no better friend for us than he; yet this too is merely a conventional practice of patience. // 3.27 //
Indeed, seeing [beings] as ruled by their own <s>karma</s>, and from seeing the virtues [of patience], one endures;

children.text: naivaṃprakārāpi hi naiṣṭhikatvaṃ kṣāntirvikalpopahatā prayāti // Ps_3.28 //
children.translated_text: but even patience of this kind, tainted by conceptualization, does not attain finality. // 3.28 //

children.text: anityaduḥkhāśuciniḥsvabhāvatā mama kṣamante na tu tadviparyayāḥ /
children.translated_text: Impermanence, suffering, impurity, and absence of self-nature are patient with me, but not their opposites;

children.text: iyaṃ vipakṣapraśamakṣamā kṣamā dvayapravṛtterna tu pāramārthikī // Ps_3.29 //
children.translated_text: this patience, capable of pacifying the adversary, arises from duality and is not ultimate. // 3.29 //
The person who, without effort, is discerning of the true meaning, engages in benefiting others;

children.text: kṣamā na caivaṃ samatāṃ sameti yā yataḥ kṣamaivaṃ na vikalpanakṣayā // Ps_3.30 //
children.translated_text: but patience does not attain equality in this way, since patience [exercised] thus is not the destruction of conceptualization. // 3.30 //
When all sequences of conceptualization — higher, equal, and lower — come to cessation without remainder,
those who walk the path of non-duality call that the unsurpassed patience beyond the range of the mind. // 3.31 //

children.text: svataḥ parasmādubhayādahetuto yathā na bhāvāḥ prabhavanti ke cana /
children.translated_text: Just as phenomena do not arise from themselves, from another, from both, or without a cause,

children.text: svataḥ parasmād ubhayād ahetutastathā na bhāvā vibhavanti ke cana // Ps_3.32 //
children.translated_text: likewise, phenomena do not perish from themselves, from another, from both, or without a cause. // 3.32 //

children.text: naṣṭād anaṣṭād ubhayāc na nobhayān na jātu kāryaṃ khalu vidyate kva cit /
children.translated_text: From what has perished, from what has not perished, from both, or from neither — no effect ever exists anywhere;

children.text: tathāpi kāryaṃ samudeti vastuno yetthaṃ kṣamā sā dvayavarjitā kṣamā // Ps_3.33 //
children.translated_text: yet effects arise from things — the patience that understands this is the patience free from duality. // 3.33 //

children.text: sato 'sato vāsti na janma janmanā vinā nirodho 'pi na kasya cit kva cit /
children.translated_text: There is no birth of what exists or what does not exist; without birth, there is no cessation of anything anywhere;

children.text: svabhāvaśūnyāmiti bhāvakalpanāṃ vipaśyataḥ kṣāntirudeti naiṣṭhikī // Ps_3.34 //
children.translated_text: for one who perceives the fabrication of phenomena as empty of intrinsic nature (<s>svabhāva-śūnya</s>), the definitive patience arises. // 3.34 //

children.text: avāpya yāṃ vyākriyate sahasraśo jinairasau nāma jino bhaviṣyati /
children.translated_text: Attaining which, one is prophesied a thousandfold by the <s>Jinas</s> (Buddhas): 'This one shall become a <s>Jina</s> named [so-and-so]';

children.text: pravartate lokahitakriyāvidhiḥ samāhitasyaiva ca tasya sarvadā // Ps_3.35 //
children.translated_text: and the performance of deeds for the welfare of the world proceeds constantly for that concentrated one. // 3.35 //
As long as the intellect is engrossed in phenomena, so long through delusion it encounters duality;

children.text: tathānimittaṃ ca vimokṣaheturdure bhavatyasya yathā kṣiteḥ kham // Ps_3.36 //
children.translated_text: and the signless (<s>animitta</s>) liberation-cause remains as far from him as the sky from the earth. // 3.36 //
He attains mastery in the acts of <s>dharma</s>-resolution, in births with flourishing liberation,

children.text: tathā pariṣkāravidhau svacetasi prakarṣiṇi jñānabale tathāyuṣi // Ps_3.37 //
children.translated_text: likewise in the method of purifying one's own mind, in the excellence of the power of knowledge, and in lifespan. // 3.37 //

children.text: avāpya caitadvaśitāmayaṃ dhanaṃ prakṛṣṭaṃ akṣiṣṇu parārthasādhanam /
children.translated_text: And attaining this mastery — this supreme, inexhaustible wealth, the means of accomplishing the welfare of others —

children.text: janasya kṛcchreṣu patiṣyataḥ sataḥ sa jāyate dhāraṇakāraṇaṃ vibhuḥ // Ps_3.38 //
children.translated_text: the powerful one is born as the cause of support for beings who are falling into misery. // 3.38 //
Therefore, by those who shoulder the great burden for the sake of others, this method of patience should always be followed;

children.text: atra sthitasya hi bhavanti parārthacittāḥ sarvā<;ḥ>; kriyā guṇaphalābharaṇābhirāmāḥ // Ps_3.39 //
children.translated_text: for one who stands in this, all actions become other-regarding, adorned with the fruit of virtues, delightful. // 3.39 //

children.text: asyāṃ hi bhaktirapi yā pravirūḍhamūlā tāmabhyasanti munayo munirājabhāve /
children.translated_text: The devotion to this [patience], deeply rooted, the sages cultivate in the state of the king of sages;

children.text: śraddhānuviddhamanasāṃ na hi dharmamārge dṛṣṭo manoratharathasya yato 'kṣabhaṅgaḥ // Ps_3.40 //
children.translated_text: for on the path of <s>dharma</s>, no breaking of the axle of the chariot of wishes has been seen for those whose minds are permeated with faith. // 3.40 //
// Summary of the <s>Kṣānti-pāramitā</s> (Perfection of Patience) //
4. Summary of the <s>Vīrya-pāramitā</s> (Perfection of Vigor)

children.text: sarvaṃsahe kṣāntibale ca rūḍhe sarvādbhutānyārabhate sa śauryāt /
children.translated_text: When the all-bearing power of patience is firmly established, he undertakes all wondrous [deeds] through valor;

children.text: vīryeṇa kāryāntamahābalena yasmāt sa devānapi yātyatītya // Ps_4.1 //
children.translated_text: through vigor of great strength that reaches the end of all tasks, he surpasses even the gods. // 4.1 //
Even worldly tasks that appear to have visible limits are difficult to overcome without vigor;

children.text: aprāpyarūpaṃ tu na kiṃ cid asti khedānabhijñena parākrameṇa // Ps_4.2 //
children.translated_text: but nothing is of unattainable form for one whose endeavor knows no weariness. // 4.2 //

children.text: ārabdham evotsahate na hīna ārabhya madhyastu viṣādameti /
children.translated_text: The inferior undertakes only what has already been begun; the middling, having begun, falls into despondency;
but those with unwearying endeavor for the sake of others, renouncing <s>nirvāṇa</s>, begin [the great work]. // 4.3 //
This world, though possessing self-dependent vigor, is mostly stricken with wretchedness, burdened with its own affairs;
but for one of undiminished vigor, even the burden of others' welfare, though firm as <s>Meru</s>, is accomplishable without weariness. // 4.4 //
If at both ends of <s>saṃsāra</s>, with equal measures of effort, there were days [as many]
as years — with immensely long <s>kalpas</s> (aeons) equal to the drops of ocean water — // 4.5 //
if with each such effort I were to generate the <s>bodhicitta</s> (awakening mind) one by one,
and were to accumulate the remaining stores of merit — even so, with weariness and wretchedness cast far aside — // 4.6 //

children.text: ekaikamevaṃ yadi bodhicittaṃ prāpyeta saṃbhāravidhiśca śeṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: if one by one the <s>bodhicitta</s> were thus attained, and the remaining accumulation of merit [completed],
even so I would bring <s>bodhi</s> (awakening) to fruition, with the essence of steadfastness energized by compassion. // 4.7 //
Without thinking of one's own suffering in <s>saṃsāra</s> — such inconceivable firmness of the armor [of resolve] —

children.text: ādyaṃ samādānamidaṃ vadanti vīravratānāṃ karuṇātmakānām // Ps_4.8 //
children.translated_text: they call this the first undertaking of those whose nature is compassion, who have taken the vow of heroes. // 4.8 //

children.text: padbhyāṃ atikramya kukūlakalpāṃ kṛtsnāṃ mahīmāyudhasaṃvṛtāṃ vā /
children.translated_text: Traversing on foot the entire earth, [harsh] as a pit of embers or covered with weapons,

children.text: yaddraṣṭum apyutsahate munīndrān pātuṃ śivaṃ dharmarasāyanaṃ vā // Ps_4.9 //
children.translated_text: if one perseveres even [merely] to see the chief of sages (<s>Munīndra</s>) or to drink the healing elixir of the auspicious <s>Dharma</s> — // 4.9a-b //
'This humanity is to be raised by me from the mire of <s>saṃsāra</s> and established in the bliss of <s>nirvāṇa</s>' —

children.text: utkṣepanikṣepavidhau padānāṃ yaccittamevaṃ ca samādadāti // Ps_4.10 //
children.translated_text: that mind which thus applies itself to the discipline of raising and placing the feet. Ps_4.10

children.text: yad vā hitārthaṃ kramate parasya puṇyāni vā lokahitāya cittam /
children.translated_text: Or that which strives for the benefit of another, or the mind that gathers merit for the welfare of the world,
that is the second <s>parākrama</s> (heroic effort) of those of inexhaustible valor, in the discipline of noble undertaking. Ps_4.11
And that which, at the very moment of the arising of merit, dedicates it toward <s>Buddhahood</s>,

children.text: tadakṣayatvaṃ samudāgamāya śubhaṃ samādānam udāharanti // Ps_4.12 //
children.translated_text: that, they declare, is the auspicious undertaking for the attainment of imperishability. Ps_4.12

children.text: mahatsu vāmbhaḥsu yathā niṣikto naivodabinduḥ kṣayamabhyupaiti /
children.translated_text: Just as a drop of water poured into a great body of water never comes to exhaustion,

children.text: saṃbuddhabhāve pariṇāmitasya tathaiva puṇyasya na saṃkṣayo 'sti // Ps_4.13 //
children.translated_text: so too there is no diminishment of merit that has been dedicated toward <s>Buddhahood</s>. Ps_4.13
For thus, with intellect purified by compassion, these merits bear fruit for the sake of <s>sarvajña</s> (omniscient) state,

children.text: puṇyāni lokasya carācarasyetyevaṃ sa tānyārabhate susattvaḥ // Ps_4.14 //
children.translated_text: for all the world, moving and unmoving — thus does that noble-souled one undertake them. Ps_4.14
No one could lead to <s>nirvāṇa</s> the mass of beings throughout the great trichiliocosm in a single day,

children.text: kalpaṃ tathā naiva ca sattvadhātostenāpi kiṃ cit paripācitaṃ syāt // Ps_4.15 //
children.translated_text: nor even in a <s>kalpa</s> (aeon); and even thereby, not even a fraction of the realm of beings would be matured. Ps_4.15

children.text: śrutvāpi sattvākṣayatāṃ imāṃ yaḥ sattvānaśeṣān vininīṣureva /
children.translated_text: He who, even upon hearing of this inexhaustibility of beings, still wishes to lead all beings without exception,
whose <s>vīrya</s> (vigor) is untouched by the flaw of despondency — how can the essence of his goal be distant? Ps_4.16
The entire mass of merit of all beings — by tenfold that measure, in a single hair-pore of the <s>Jina</s> (Victor),
it reaches cessation, each single well-born hair in each single pore. Ps_4.17

children.text: śatena bhūyo guṇitena tena puṇyena romāspadasaṃśritena /
children.translated_text: By that merit multiplied a hundredfold further, residing in the site of a single hair,

children.text: bhavatyanuvyañjanamekameva śeṣāṇi tasya prabhavanti kāye // Ps_4.18 //
children.translated_text: a single <s>anuvyañjana</s> (minor mark) comes into being; and the rest manifest upon his body. Ps_4.18
And from a mass of merit of that same multiplied measure, arising from that <s>anuvyañjana</s>,
each of the <s>lakṣaṇas</s> (major marks) proclaiming his <s>Jinahood</s> is brought forth as a wondrous design. Ps_4.19
And from the merit that is the cause for the arising of those excellent <s>lakṣaṇas</s>, multiplied by thousands,
there arises his <s>ūrṇā</s> (tuft between the brows), of delightful color, with a radiance as brilliant as the full moon. Ps_4.20
And the merit that brings forth the <s>ūrṇā</s>, multiplied by a hundred thousands,
produces his <s>uṣṇīṣa</s> (crown protuberance), the crest of his head, resplendent as a parasol, beyond compare. Ps_4.21

children.text: ayaṃ mayā puṇyanidhiḥ parārthaṃ saṃceya ityuttamabodhicitte /
children.translated_text: Thinking 'This treasury of merit has been accumulated by me for the sake of others,' with his mind turned toward supreme <s>bodhicitta</s> (awakening mind),

children.text: vīryonmukhe kena mukhena tasmiṃllayapravṛttirlabhatāṃ praveśam // Ps_4.22 //
children.translated_text: facing <s>vīrya</s> (vigor) — through what avenue could lassitude gain entry into that? Ps_4.22

children.text: sarve 'pi sattvā yadi lokadhātau pratyekabuddhaiḥ sadṛśā bhaveyuḥ /
children.translated_text: Even if all beings in the world-realm were equal to <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>,

children.text: jñānena tebhyo 'bhyadhikaprabhāvaḥ kṣāntistha eko 'pi hi bodhisattvaḥ // Ps_4.23 //
children.translated_text: even a single <s>bodhisattva</s> established in <s>kṣānti</s> (patience) surpasses them in the power of <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge). Ps_4.23
And likewise, one who is irreversible surpasses those established in the strength of <s>kṣānti</s> (patience),

children.text: aśrāntavīryaḥ kuśalaprayoge yallaukike caiva taduttare ca // Ps_4.24 //
children.translated_text: being of unwearied <s>vīrya</s> (vigor) in wholesome practice, both worldly and supramundane. Ps_4.24

children.text: tebhyaḥ puṇaścādhika eva dūraṃ ya ekajātipratibaddhabodhiḥ /
children.translated_text: And again, far superior even to those is one whose <s>bodhi</s> (awakening) is bound to a single birth;

children.text: ka eva vādo dṛḍhavīryavatsu ye bodhimūle prathamaṃ niṣaṇṇāḥ // Ps_4.25 //
children.translated_text: what need to speak of those of firm <s>vīrya</s> (vigor) who have first seated themselves at the foot of the <s>Bodhi</s> tree? Ps_4.25
Even if the entire world-realm were filled with those of such purity of <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge),

children.text: yāyāt kalāṃ so 'pi na bodhimūle sthitasya mārātikṛtāntyajāteḥ // Ps_4.26 //
children.translated_text: it would not reach even a fraction of the one seated at the <s>Bodhi</s> tree, the vanquisher of <s>Māra</s>, in his final birth. Ps_4.26
Even if all worlds without exception were filled with those of such purity of mind through <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge),

children.text: balapradeśasya muneratulyāḥ kalāpradeśairapi te samagrāḥ // Ps_4.27 //
children.translated_text: all of them together would be unequal even to a fraction of the <s>Muni's</s> (Sage's) strength. Ps_4.27
Thus, alone, one of compassionate nature strives to cross this wondrous ocean of <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge),

children.text: avyāhatājñaḥ paracittacāre prajñāvabhāsaṃ ca nabho viśālam // Ps_4.28 //
children.translated_text: unobstructed in knowing the minds of others, and illuminating the sky-vast radiance of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom). Ps_4.28

children.text: sarveṣu sattveṣu ca tasya mātrā samānahārdā karuṇābhyudeti /
children.translated_text: And toward all beings, his <s>karuṇā</s> (compassion) arises with equal affection, like that of a parent,
and from that, all the remaining wondrous <s>Buddhadharmas</s> (qualities of a Buddha) come into being without exception. Ps_4.29
Endowed with these qualities of undertaking, with pure streams of hearing, with beings of gentle nature,
like the eightfold path to truth, the path shines forth supremely through the excellence of <s>vīrya</s> (vigor). Ps_4.30
<s>Vīrya</s> (vigor) is threefold as wholesome practice, and from that arise the distinctions of speech, body, and mind,
of the excellence of <s>vīrya</s> (vigor) that is mental in nature, in its stages of setting forth, abiding, and concentration. Ps_4.31

children.text: yo bodhicittapraṇayaḥ samaśca kṛpā ca nairātmagatau kṣamā ca /
children.translated_text: The devotion to <s>bodhicitta</s> (awakening mind) and equanimity, <s>kṛpā</s> (compassion) and patient acceptance of selflessness,
the fourfold <s>saṃgraha</s> (means of gathering disciples) and non-attachment to all <s>dharmas</s> (phenomena), Ps_4.32

children.text: saṃsārapaṅke yadakhinnatā ca traidhātukasyaiva ca nopalabdhiḥ /
children.translated_text: unweariness in the mire of <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence), and the non-apprehension of the triple realm,

children.text: sarvasvadānaṃ na ca tena mānaḥ samagraśikṣasya na śikṣayā ca // Ps_4.33 //
children.translated_text: the giving of all one possesses without pride in that, and for one of complete training, no attachment to training, Ps_4.33
the steadfastness of mind unaltered by the harms of others, and the utter non-distraction of the mind,

children.text: ārambhadārḍhayaṃ kuśalakriyāsu prītirvivekaikarasā ca citte // Ps_4.34 //
children.translated_text: firmness in undertaking wholesome deeds, and the mind's delight whose sole savor is solitude, Ps_4.34
the attainment of the four kinds of <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), the mind's realization of selflessness,
insatiable desire for the expanse of learning, and penetration of right reasoning through investigation, Ps_4.35

children.text: yā deśanā caiva yathāśrutānāṃ jñānaṃ ca dharmānabhilāpyatāyām /
children.translated_text: the teaching of what has been heard, and <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge) of the inexpressibility of <s>dharmas</s> (phenomena),

children.text: pañcasvabhijñāsu ca yatprabhutvam abhyāsamātrā ca taduttarāyām // Ps_4.36 //
children.translated_text: mastery over the five <s>abhijñās</s> (superknowledges), and the practice that leads to the supreme one beyond those, Ps_4.36

children.text: yadṛddhipādeṣvabhinirhṛtatvaṃ paṭvī na cāyāsamayī kriyā ca /
children.translated_text: the accomplishment in the <s>ṛddhipādas</s> (bases of supernatural power), and action that is swift and effortless,

children.text: samyakprahāṇeṣu ca yaḥ prayogaḥ śubhāśubhādeva ca yā vimuktiḥ // Ps_4.37 //
children.translated_text: the practice of the <s>samyakprahāṇas</s> (right exertions), and liberation from what is wholesome and unwholesome alike, Ps_4.37

children.text: yatkauśalaṃ cendriyanirṇayeṣu nirindriyān paśyati yacca dharmān /
children.translated_text: skill in the discernment of the <s>indriyas</s> (faculties), and seeing <s>dharmas</s> (phenomena) as without faculties,

children.text: mārgasya saṃbhāravimārgaṇaṃ ca na cāsya kiṃ cid gamanaṃ kutaścit // Ps_4.38 //
children.translated_text: the seeking of the provisions of the path, and yet there being no going anywhere from anything — Ps_4.38
thus, this vast and manifold <s>vīrya</s> (vigor), varied in its stages of setting forth and abiding,
for the purpose of filling its inexhaustibility, the very act of setting forth is the special cause. Ps_4.39

children.text: nimittakarmasvapi na pravartate vitiṣṭhate jñānamaye ca karmaṇi /
children.translated_text: One does not engage in sign-making activities, and abides in action that is of the nature of <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge);

children.text: kṛpāguṇādyan na jahāti saṃskṛtaṃ na coruvīryo 'pi patatyasaṃskṛte // Ps_4.40 //
children.translated_text: due to the quality of <s>kṛpā</s> (compassion), one does not abandon the conditioned, nor does one of great <s>vīrya</s> (vigor) fall into the unconditioned. Ps_4.40
Hearing of <s>Dharma</s> previously unheard, freedom from illness, being difficult to overcome, retaining the <s>Dharma</s> heard,

children.text: amānuṣebhyo 'pi parigrahodayaḥ samādhigotrapratilambha eva ca // Ps_4.41 //
children.translated_text: the arising of support even from non-human beings, and the very attainment of the lineage of <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) — Ps_4.41

children.text: vrajantyavandhyā yadaharniśaṃ kriyā guṇairna hāniṃ yadutpaiti mauśalīm /
children.translated_text: when deeds performed day and night are never fruitless, when one's virtues suffer no collective decline,
and when one's virtues flourish ever more like a lotus, with purposes surpassing human norms — Ps_4.42

children.text: yaśo viśālam ca sukhaṃ sukhodayaṃ vinītakārpaṇyamanastvamuttamam /
children.translated_text: widespread fame, happiness that gives rise to happiness, the supreme state of mind freed from wretchedness,

children.text: guṇāśca teṣāmiha dṛṣṭadhārmikā bhavanti vīryāditi ko 'tra vismayaḥ // Ps_4.43 //
children.translated_text: these are the visible fruits of <s>vīrya</s> (vigor) in this very life — what wonder is there in this? Ps_4.43
When persons firmly supported by the activity of <s>vīrya</s> (vigor) attain even <s>Buddhahood</s>,

children.text: vīryavyāpāśrayadṛḍhāḥ puruṣā na syād ataḥ ka iva vīryaparaḥ // Ps_4.44 //
children.translated_text: worshipped by the three worlds, endowed with immeasurable and great virtues — who then would not be devoted to <s>vīrya</s> (vigor)? Ps_4.44
Thus ends the Summary of the Perfection of <s>Vīrya</s> (Vigor).
5. Summary of the Perfection of <s>Dhyāna</s> (Meditation)
Now one should apply oneself to the discipline of <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) for the increase of <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge),

children.text: sukhaṃ hi kartuṃ lokānāṃ jñānālokādanugraham // Ps_5.1 //
children.translated_text: for it is easy to bestow upon the worlds the grace that comes from the light of <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge). Ps_5.1
<s>Jñāna</s> (knowledge) becomes exceedingly clear through <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) in a purified mind,
like the disc of the moon in the autumn sky when the clouds have been dispersed. Ps_5.2
One of purified <s>śīla</s> (moral conduct), accompanied by virtuous and beneficial companions,
with few duties, with a tranquil self, girded with the foundation of <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness), Ps_5.3
dwelling at the roots of trees, on grounds spread with green grass,
in places of natural beauty, fragrant with forest flowers, Ps_5.4
in abodes conducive to the companionship of <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), inhabited by contented people,
which seem to stand in profound stillness due to the silence of their inhabitants, Ps_5.5
in hermitages set apart in the forest, or in empty sanctuaries,
or in the caves of mountains, resounding with the roar of lions, Ps_5.6

children.text: yatra kva cana vā deśe saṃsargakleśavarjite /
children.translated_text: or in whatever place free from the defilement of worldly association,

children.text: paryaṅkena sukhāsīnaḥ śarīram ṛju dhārayan // Ps_5.7 //
children.translated_text: seated comfortably in the cross-legged posture, holding the body upright, Ps_5.7
having established the guard of <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness) facing the heart,
having, as it were, by <s>kṛpā</s> (compassion), proclaimed the inauspiciousness of evil thoughts, Ps_5.8

children.text: prajñāparicayasyāyāṃ kālo me na tu nirvṛteḥ /
children.translated_text: 'This is my time for the cultivation of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), not for quiescence;

children.text: na hi sattvān anirvāpya svayaṃ nirvātum utsahe // Ps_5.9 //
children.translated_text: for I do not aspire to attain <s>nirvāṇa</s> myself without first having led beings to liberation' — Ps_5.9
thus, watching over the welfare of the world, with longing directed toward <s>Buddhahood</s>,
one should with continuous practice make the effort to undertake <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation). Ps_5.10
For one who rests and rests again while churning will not obtain fire;

children.text: sa eva yogo yoge 'pi viśeṣādhigamādṛte // Ps_5.11 //
children.translated_text: that very same principle applies to <s>yoga</s> (meditative practice) as well, with regard to the attainment of higher stages. Ps_5.11

children.text: ekatraiva ca badhnīyād dṛḍham ālambane manaḥ /
children.translated_text: One should bind the mind firmly to a single object of concentration;
grasping at various objects only afflicts the mind with agitation. Ps_5.12
When the mind sinks away, one should lift it up through insight and the strength of <s>vīrya</s> (vigor);

children.text: uddhanyamānaṃ ca manaḥ praśamena nivārayet // Ps_5.13 //
children.translated_text: and one should restrain the agitated mind through tranquility. // Ps_5.13 //
Rightly directed, equanimous, and unwavering through the power of <s>samādhi</s> (concentration),

children.text: tatrāpi vā tanmayaḥ syāt sugatajñānalabdhaye // Ps_5.14 //
children.translated_text: one should become absorbed in that very state for the attainment of the <s>Sugata</s>'s (Well-Gone One's) wisdom. // Ps_5.14 //
One should not let the relishing of <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) bliss lead to dependency,
for this extensive undertaking is not merely for the sake of one's own pleasure. // Ps_5.15 //
Even with concern for body and life, even with a mind afflicted by misery,
one should not slacken in vigor, even if one's own head were ablaze. // Ps_5.16 //
Having observed the signs for the <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) of that mind,
when it is slipping away, one should again apply it with attentive <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness). // Ps_5.17 //
One should turn the mind away from the <s>nīvaraṇas</s> (hindrances) by means of their antidotes,
as one would restrain a self-willed elephant with the pulls of a goad. // Ps_5.18 //
Then, with a mind restored to health by the destruction of the disease of the <s>nīvaraṇas</s> (hindrances),
as if freed from poverty, as if released from a great calamity, // Ps_5.19 //
with a mind filled with joy, one should reflect on the faults of <s>kāma</s> (sensual desires),
and on the supreme succession of happiness obtained through separation from them. // Ps_5.20 //
Fickle as the flash of lightning, of the nature of foam and garments,
with pleasures as insubstantial as dreams, arisen as if for the purpose of deception, // Ps_5.21 //
even parents toward children, and children toward parents,
even dear friends toward those for whom affection is everything, // Ps_5.22 //
even in hard-fought battles, where one bound by an accumulation of virtues
has displayed the essence of steadfastness — these desires tear asunder the bridge of affection. // Ps_5.23 //
Since <s>kāmas</s> (sensual desires) are the cause of the suffering of pursuit in this life

children.text: hetubhūtā yataḥ kāmāḥ kāmayeta na tān ataḥ // Ps_5.24 //
children.translated_text: and of hell in the next, therefore one should not desire them. // Ps_5.24 //
Since even conceptual thought (<s>vitarka</s>), whose basis is desire, closes the eye of wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>),
and operates for the destruction of both oneself and others, // Ps_5.25 //
and since even those who desire their own welfare completely abandon them,
how could one who desires the welfare of others, having renounced those desires, recall them? // Ps_5.26 //
There is no satisfaction from them through attainment, nor through daily indulgence,

children.text: naiva saṃnicayenāpi ko 'nyo vyādhirataḥ paraḥ // Ps_5.27 //
children.translated_text: nor even through accumulation — what other disease is worse than this? // Ps_5.27 //
Since one struck by their taste does not even comprehend one's own welfare,
what wise person would recall those desires, which are like the drink of a madman? // Ps_5.28 //
Thus, as one perceives desires to be thoroughly corrupt in every way,
the mind, having contracted from them, becomes serene in renunciation (<s>naiṣkramya</s>). // Ps_5.29 //
Then one attains the joy and happiness born of seclusion (<s>viveka</s>), born of tranquility (<s>praśrabdhi</s>),
the one-pointedness of mind known as the first <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation). // Ps_5.30 //
That practitioner, seeing the corruption of <s>vitarka</s> (applied thought) and <s>vicāra</s> (sustained thought) as one sees that of desires,
seeking their pacification, cultivates the happiness born of the joy of <s>samādhi</s> (concentration). // Ps_5.31 //
Through inner clarity (<s>adhyātmasaṃprasāda</s>) and one-pointedness of mind,
that is declared to be the second <s>dhyāna</s> by the peerless great sages (<s>maharṣis</s>). // Ps_5.32 //

children.text: utplavaṃ manaso dṛṣṭvā prīteratha virajya saḥ /
children.translated_text: Then, having seen the agitation of the mind caused by joy (<s>prīti</s>), and becoming dispassionate toward it,
