one attains the third <s>dhyāna</s>, endowed with <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness) and <s>upekṣā</s> (equanimity). // Ps_5.33 //
Abandoning even the enjoyment of happiness, with both pleasure and pain eliminated,
purified by <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness) and <s>upekṣā</s> (equanimity), one reaches the fourth <s>dhyāna</s>. // Ps_5.34 //

children.text: abhijñā labhate pañca sa ca tatrānugāminīḥ /
children.translated_text: And there one obtains the five <s>abhijñās</s> (super-knowledges) that follow upon that state,
like a righteous king established in his kingdom obtains modesty, fame, glory, intelligence, and radiance. // Ps_5.35 //
And surpassing those obtained by <s>pratyekabuddhas</s> (solitary awakened ones) and those of the <s>śrāvakas</s> (disciples),
these become far superior, due to their accomplishment of the welfare of others. // Ps_5.36 //
For the <s>bodhisattva</s> guides the miserly toward generosity (<s>dāna</s>), those deficient in morality toward <s>śīla</s> (moral conduct),
the wrathful toward patience (<s>kṣānti</s>) and gentleness, the indolent toward the attainment of vigor (<s>vīrya</s>), // Ps_5.37 //
those of scattered mind toward <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), and those bereft of it toward <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom),
out of compassion (<s>kāruṇya</s>), with untiring effort in practice. // Ps_5.38 //
Therefore, with unfailing, blazing rays, illuminating the worlds
like the rays of the sun, one creates a boundless domain of action. // Ps_5.39 //
Then, seeing beings who have done evil falling into hells and other realms,
and gods whose merit and lifespan are exhausted yet who consider themselves eternal, // Ps_5.40 //
and the world afflicted by causation through various particular sufferings,

children.text: tatra divyaprabhāveṇa cakṣuṣā sā vilokayan // Ps_5.41 //
children.translated_text: beholding all this with the divine eye (<s>divyacakṣus</s>) through supernatural power, // Ps_5.41 //
one arrives at intense compassion (<s>kāruṇya</s>); from compassion, one does not become heedless,
and being vigilant in the welfare of others, one attains inconceivable power. // Ps_5.42 //
Then one beholds the <s>Tathāgatas</s> (Thus-Gone Ones) dwelling in other world-systems,
the arrays of virtues of their <s>buddhakṣetras</s> (buddha-fields), and the excellences of the <s>saṃgha</s> (community). // Ps_5.43 //
And one perceives the pure conduct and domain of the supreme <s>bodhisattvas</s>,
their glorious deeds whose purpose is the benefit of all the world. // Ps_5.44 //
And there, one's aspiration (<s>praṇidhi</s>) is easily fulfilled,
through the transformation for the benefit of others and the excellence of one's <s>śīla</s> (moral conduct). // Ps_5.45 //
With the superhuman, divine hearing (<s>divyaśrotra</s>) that is pure in meaning,
one hears various utterances, even from afar as if they were near, // Ps_5.46 //
words spoken in the distance by those moved by compassion (<s>kṛpā</s>), with harsh and unpleasant syllables,
like flames issuing from a fire of anger blazing within. // Ps_5.47 //
The songs of <s>apsarases</s> (celestial nymphs) as companions, ornaments resounding with their tinkling,
and the sounds of divine instruments, all of a single essence of destruction, // Ps_5.48 //
indulged in by those blinded by passion — enemies in the guise of friends —

children.text: vīkṣya vrajati kāruṇyaṃ teṣāṃ vāñcanayā tayā // Ps_5.49 //
children.translated_text: seeing this, one is moved to compassion (<s>kāruṇya</s>) with the wish to save them. // Ps_5.49 //
And then, struck in the heart as it were by the anguished cries of hell-beings,
with words and syllables rendered indistinct by fear and particular sufferings, // Ps_5.50 //
one of great compassion (<s>mahākṛpā</s>), penetrating to the marrow, summons supreme vigor (<s>vīrya</s>),

children.text: tīkṣṇāgreṇa pratodena sadaśva iva coditaḥ // Ps_5.51 //
children.translated_text: like a fine horse spurred by a sharp-pointed goad. // Ps_5.51 //
Then one hears from the <s>Jinas</s> (Victorious Ones) abiding in various world-systems
the inexhaustible <s>Dharma</s> teachings, inspired by the aspiration for <s>nirvāṇa</s> of all beings. // Ps_5.52 //
Then, discerning in the minds of others their latent tendencies (<s>anuśaya</s>) and dispositions (<s>āśaya</s>),
one plants the seeds of merit, which are the provisions and means for knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>). // Ps_5.53 //
And recollecting former abodes (<s>pūrvanivāsa</s>) through tens of millions of <s>kalpas</s> (cosmic ages),
seeing the merits of beings, and likewise the strength and weakness of their faculties (<s>indriyas</s>), // Ps_5.54 //
through the supernatural power (<s>ṛddhi</s>) dependent on that basis, having multiplied one's form,
one's discourse is never fruitless, since one teaches according to the vessel. // Ps_5.55 //
Somewhere, with a body whose splendor of beauty is not belied even by the radiance of a thousand suns,
bearing the marks of a lord of sages (<s>munirāja</s>), with clearly variegated auspicious signs, // Ps_5.56 //
creating a festival for the eyes of people, bringing special delight through speech,
one illuminates the <s>amṛta</s> (deathless nectar) for the attainment of <s>Jinahood</s> (Buddhahood) among those devoted to the <s>Jinas</s>. // Ps_5.57 //
Somewhere, with the splendor of a sage (<s>muniśrī</s>) supreme in tranquility, with conduct distinguished by profound meaning,
assuming the form of a sage's disciple, one tames those whose minds are fit for training. // Ps_5.58 //
With lotus feet worshipped by the crest-jewels of gods, like great <s>Indra</s>,

children.text: dhanado dhanado yathā kva cit kuha cidbrahmavadadbhutadyutiḥ // Ps_5.59 //
children.translated_text: somewhere like <s>Dhanada</s> (<s>Kubera</s>, lord of wealth), somewhere like <s>Brahmā</s> of wondrous radiance, // Ps_5.59 //
somewhere with three eyes open, with the pure crescent moon as head-ornament,
with radiance blazing like the lord of the immortals, somewhere bearing the splendor of <s>Bhujagendrā</s> (the serpent king), // Ps_5.60 //
somewhere with fingers tawny as thunderbolt-fire, like the king of kings <s>Guhyaka</s>,

children.text: amitājinalakṣmavān kva cid guṇaraśmirmunicandramā iva // Ps_5.61 //
children.translated_text: somewhere bearing the mark of <s>Amitājina</s> (<s>Amitābha</s>), like a moon among sages emitting rays of virtue, // Ps_5.61 //
with radiance blazing from the broad chest through the bright rays of the <s>Kaustubha</s> gem,

children.text: garuḍadhvajarājadṛk kva cit kuha ciccaiva halāyudhadyutiḥ // Ps_5.62 //
children.translated_text: somewhere appearing as the king with <s>Garuḍa</s>-banner, somewhere with the radiance of <s>Halāyudha</s> (<s>Balarāma</s>), // Ps_5.62 //
somewhere bearing a white spear, of inconceivable power, with a beautiful peacock as vehicle,
somewhere with form pure as the moon and sun, adorned with the mountains of rising and setting. // Ps_5.63 //
Somewhere with the body of the <s>Maruts</s> (wind gods) who have abandoned food, elsewhere of those who feed on human beings,

children.text: vāruṇadyutim udvahan kva cit kuha cinmanmathacāruvigrahaḥ // Ps_5.64 //
children.translated_text: somewhere bearing the radiance of <s>Varuṇa</s>, somewhere with the beautiful form of <s>Manmatha</s> (the god of love), // Ps_5.64 //
taking on the graceful form of a woman, captivating through the pleasure of union between men and women,

children.text: kva cid eva tapodhanaśriyaṃ vidadhat kāmaviraktamānasaḥ // Ps_5.65 //
children.translated_text: and somewhere else displaying the splendor of an ascetic (<s>tapodhana</s>), with a mind free from desire. // Ps_5.65 //
Somewhere captivating the hearts of people through the conduct of a teacher, disciple, or king,
and even in the hells, through the power of transformation, creating the moment of liberation from suffering. // Ps_5.66 //
Then, through various extensive manifestations corresponding to the dispositions (<s>adhimukti</s>) of beings,
endowed with the continuity of the quality of compassion (<s>karuṇā</s>), one creates the welfare of the world here and there. // Ps_5.67 //
Having attained this extensive, distinguished excellence through the qualities of <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation),
one should strive all the more, as one does when signs of treasure prove trustworthy. // Ps_5.68 //
Even an unstrengthened abiding in virtue — what harm can come from it, accustomed as it is to relaxed vows?

children.text: prayateta vivṛddhaye tataḥ parihāṇistu viparyayādataḥ // Ps_5.69 //
sahasā vijigīṣuṇā yathā vijitasya praśamapratikriyā // Ps_5.70 //
manasaḥ parivṛttilāghavaṃ paramaṃ tatra na viśvasedataḥ /
vyatiyāti tu māragocaraṃ tamanarthaṃ praśamayya sarvathā // Ps_5.74 //
calatānugato hi niśrayaḥ sakhaṭuṅkastata eva kathyate // Ps_5.75 //
na hi kiṃ cid udeti kutra cit sadasatsaṃbhavayuktyasaṃbhavāt // Ps_5.76 //
kurute sa ca laukikīṃ kriyāṃ jagadekāntahitānuvartinīm /
na samādhibalācca hīyate vaśavartitvamavāpya cetasaḥ // Ps_5.78 //
kriyāsu sāmarthyaguṇaṃ hi teṣāṃ prajñaiva vistāriṇamādadhāti /
tathaiva kāryāṇi na bhānti loke prajñāviyogena jadīkṛtāni // Ps_6.3 //
guṇāguṇān vetti hi tatsanāthaḥ kleśakṣaye naipuṇametyataśca // Ps_6.4 //
tyāgaṃ parārthaṃ hi vadanti dānaṃ śeṣastu vṛddhyārthamiva prayogaḥ // Ps_6.5 //
naivonnatiṃ nāvanatiṃ prayānti bhaiṣajyavṛkṣā iva nirviklapāḥ // Ps_6.6 //
tataḥ paraṃ kāmiṣu daivateṣu loke 'pi ca dvitrisahasrasaṃkhye /
aiśvaryamāpnoti tataḥ paraṃ ca bhūmiṃ viśodhya prabhavāṃ prabhāyāḥ // Ps_6.10 //
śīlasya śuddhiḥ kuta eva tasya yaḥ prajñayā nāpahṛtāndhakāraḥ /
prāyeṇa śīlāni hi tadviyogād āmarṣadoṣaiḥ kaluṣīkriyante // Ps_6.11 //
nātmārthamapyasti tu yasya śīlaṃ prājñasya tasyāsti kathaṃ parārtham /
yo dṛṣṭadoṣo bhavabandhanānāṃ lokān samastāṃstata ujjihīrṣuḥ // Ps_6.12 //
prajñāvipakṣairhṛdi soparāge kṣamāguṇaḥ kena dhṛtiṃ labheta /
guṇāguṇāavekṣaṇakātarākṣe khyāto guṇairvīrā iva kṣitīśe // Ps_6.13 //
prajñānvitānāṃ tu parāpakārāḥ kṣamāguṇāḥ sthairyakarā bhavanti /
bhadrātmakānāmiva vāraṇānāṃ karamāśrayā naikavidhā viṣeṣāḥ // Ps_6.14 //
niṣkevalaṃ vīryamapi śramāya prajñāsanāthasya tu tasya kārye /
anuttaraḥ siddhiguṇo 'bhyudeti hartā tadutthasya pariśramasya // Ps_6.15 //
yasmāt paraṃ sūkṣamataraṃ na kiṃ cid yannaipuṇānāṃ paramaḥ prakarṣaḥ /
yatkāmadoṣādibhirāvṛtānāṃ manaḥpathaṃ naiva kadā cideti // Ps_6.16 //
prajñānirudyogamaterhi dṛṣṭirnāyāti śuddhiṃ tadṛte na śīlam /
samyakasmādhis tadṛte na labhyo duḥkhakṣayastadvirahāttathaiva // Ps_6.18 //
prājñastu doṣādbhayamīkṣamāṇaḥ sukhānubaddhaṃ ca sukhaṃ guṇebhyaḥ /
vihāya doṣāñjagadarthakāmo guṇābhirāmeṇa pathā prayāti // Ps_6.19 //
ato 'navadyena balena yuktaḥ pravartate lokahitodayeṣu // Ps_6.20 //
naiṣkāraṇorjasvalayā ca vṛttyā parārthacaryāsu samaṃ samantāt // Ps_6.21 //
sāmānyamartheṣu ca darśayitvā premṇā vaśīkṛtya manāṃsi teṣām /
bhayāni sarvāṇi hi doṣajāni prajñā na doṣaiḥ sahavāsameti /
nāmaikaśeṣāṇi karoti tāni prajñāprabhāyāḥ prasaraprabhāvaḥ // Ps_6.25 //
na tatra bhūyaḥ karaṇīyam asti yatra prabhā sā balatāmupaiti /
yugāntakālānalasaṃhṛte hi loke na dagdhavyakathāḥ prathante // Ps_6.26 //
saṃpūrṇatāṃ yāti sukhena śikṣā śīlāya cittapraśamāya caiva /
prajñābalaṃ dīptataraprabhāvaṃ nālaṃ prasoḍhuṃ sabalo 'pi māraḥ /
prajñāṃśavo vibhramayānti cakṣurna draṣṭum īśo hi yataḥ sa eva // Ps_6.31 //
adhīrasātmyaṃ bhayaviklavaṃ vā mūḍhocitaṃ śokaparigrahaṃ vā /
dīneṣu kārpaṇyamalīmasatvaṃ kṛtāspadaṃ rāgiṣu cāpalaṃ vā /

children.translated_text: And those various subtle remnants of faults, hidden in the recesses of diverse mental dispositions,

children.text: samudbhavantyeva parākaroti prajñā pratijñeva jagaddhitārthā // Ps_6.35 //
children.translated_text: are thoroughly overcome by <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) as they arise, like a vow dedicated to the welfare of the world. Ps_6.35
Having directed upon that existence the auspicious gaze of wisdom, steadfast and gentle in the destruction of faults,

children.text: svayaṃ munīndrairabhiṣicyate yat prahlādinā vyākaraṇāmṛtena // Ps_6.36 //
children.translated_text: one is anointed by the lords of sages themselves with the gladdening nectar of <s>vyākaraṇa</s> (prophecy). Ps_6.36
And by the rays of the <s>ūrṇā</s> (hair-tuft) of the great sages, laughing with the brilliance of the moon at midnight,
one shines like the sacrificial fire anointed on the crown with streams of clarified butter. Ps_6.37

children.text: avāpya yasmān muniyauvarājyaṃ samaṃ samantād visṛtātmabhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having thereby attained the prince-regency of a sage, with one's being extended equally in all directions,

children.text: lokasya duḥkhaṃ praśamatyayatnād rajo mahāmegha iva pravṛṣṭaḥ // Ps_6.38 //
children.translated_text: one effortlessly pacifies the suffering of the world, like a great cloud that has begun to rain settling the dust. Ps_6.38
All that splendor of the radiance of the sons of the <s>Sugata</s> (the Well-Gone One) is brought about by the power of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom);

children.text: ko vismayo vātra sutapriyāyā mātuḥ samīyādyadiyaṃ vibhūtiḥ // Ps_6.39 //
children.translated_text: what wonder is there in this, if such glory should belong to a mother who is dear to her children? Ps_6.39
When the tenfold powers of the sages, depending on that very <s>prajñā</s> as their basis,
arise in their supreme excellence, uniquely beautiful, along with the remaining innumerable heap of quality-gems — Ps_6.40
the <s>śāstras</s> (scriptures) that are like eyes for the world, the special arts that are like treasuries,

children.text: mantrān paritrāṇakṛto vicitrān dharmavyavasthāśca pṛthagviśeṣāḥ // Ps_6.41 //
children.translated_text: the various <s>mantras</s> that serve as protection, and the diverse particular establishments of <s>dharma</s> — Ps_6.41

children.text: paryāyacitraṃ ca vimokṣamārgaṃ tattacca lokasya hitopapādi /
children.translated_text: and the path of liberation, variegated with diverse approaches, and whatever else is conducive to the welfare of the world —

children.text: yadbodhisattvāḥ pravidarśayanti prajñāprabhāvābhyudayaḥ sa sarvaḥ // Ps_6.42 //
children.translated_text: all that which the <s>bodhisattvas</s> reveal is the arising of the power of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom). Ps_6.42
For <s>bodhisattvas</s>, even in the state of kings, with sense objects rivaling the divine,

children.text: na yadvirūpāṃ prakṛtiṃ vrajanti prajñā guṇāmātyasanāthatā sā // Ps_6.43 //
children.translated_text: do not fall into a debased nature — that is the minister-like guardianship of the quality of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom). Ps_6.43
<s>Maitrī</s> (loving-kindness), whose sole essence is benefiting others, free from the stain of passion,

children.text: parasya duḥkheṣu parā dayā ca na śokabhārālasatāṃ gatā ca // Ps_6.44 //
children.translated_text: and supreme compassion (<s>dayā</s>) for the sufferings of others, not rendered sluggish by the burden of grief, Ps_6.44
the absence of elation even when the mind is joyful, equanimity free from the onset of darkness,

children.text: te te guṇā<;ś>;cābhyadhikaṃ vibhānti prajñāniruddhapratipakṣamārgāḥ // Ps_6.45 //
children.translated_text: these and other qualities shine forth exceedingly, their opposing paths blocked by <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom). Ps_6.45

children.text: ko nāma lokasya parārthasādhurduḥkhaikahetūni tamāṃsi hanyāt /
children.translated_text: Who in the world, devoted to the welfare of others, could destroy the darknesses that are the sole cause of suffering,

children.text: avyāhatā jñānaśayāśayeṣu prajñā na cet syādatisūryādīptiḥ // Ps_6.46 //
children.translated_text: if <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), unobstructed, with radiance surpassing the sun, were not present in the disposition toward knowledge? Ps_6.46

children.text: tatprāptaye śrutam aśītivikalpacitraṃ saṃceyam āśrayasahaṃ gurumabhyupetya /
children.translated_text: To attain that, one should approach a teacher and accumulate learning, rich with eighty kinds of conceptual elaboration, bearing it in one's very being;

children.text: dvātriṃśatā tadadhigamya vivardhayeta samyaṅmanaḥ samavadhānakṛtairviśeṣaiḥ // Ps_6.47 //
children.translated_text: and having mastered those thirty-two, one should cultivate the mind with the distinctions produced by right concentration. Ps_6.47

children.text: alpaśruto 'ndha iva vetti na bhāvanāyā mārgaṃ vicintayati kāni ca tadvihīnaḥ /
children.translated_text: One of little learning, blind as it were, does not know the path of meditation, and being devoid of it, what can one contemplate?

children.text: tasmācchrutaṃ prati yateta tadāśrayā hi prajñā samudbhavati cintanabhāvanābhyām // Ps_6.48 //
children.translated_text: Therefore one should strive for learning, for <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), based on that, arises through reflection (<s>cintana</s>) and meditation (<s>bhāvanā</s>). Ps_6.48
Through questions, through discussions free from contention, through investigation and the examination of the meaning of things, and by oneself,

children.text: prajñāvivṛddhimabhitaḥ prayateta nityaṃ dhyānena tadguṇavivṛddhikareṇa caiva // Ps_6.49 //
children.translated_text: one should always strive on all sides for the growth of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), and also through <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) which promotes the growth of its qualities. Ps_6.49
This, in brief, is the method of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) and skillful means: <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) devoted to that purpose, and the detailed study of scripture;

children.text: tābhyāṃ samudbhavati hi prabhavo guṇānāṃ prajñāprabhāsamudayo 'gnirivāraṇībhyāṃ // Ps_6.50 //
children.translated_text: for from these two arises the splendor of qualities — the dawn of the light of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), like fire from the two fire-sticks. Ps_6.50
And by resorting to the path followed by the learned, one should avoid the thickets that cause delusion;

children.text: tairāvṛto na hi vibhātyudayasthito 'pi toyāvalambijaladāntaritaḥ śaśīva // Ps_6.51 //
children.translated_text: for when covered by those, one does not shine even though arisen, like the moon concealed by water-bearing clouds. Ps_6.51
Laziness, yawning mindlessness, bad companions, excessive sleepiness, and the habit of irresolution,
the cessation of eagerness for knowledge as a sage would have, and questions contracted by false pride — Ps_6.52
and timidity in approaching the learned, born from self-tormenting despondency,

children.text: mithyāvikalpapaṭutā vitathā ca dṛṣṭirmohāya tatpraśamanāya tu tadvipakṣāḥ // Ps_6.53 //
children.translated_text: cleverness in false conceptualization, and erroneous views — these lead to delusion; their opposites lead to its pacification. Ps_6.53

children.text: skandheṣu sāyatanadhātuṣu satyayuktyo<;r>; hetudbhaveṣu śucayānavinirṇaye ca /
children.translated_text: Skill in the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), <s>āyatanas</s> (sense bases), <s>dhātus</s> (elements), the truths, that which arises from causes, and in the determination of purity,

children.text: dharmeṣu kauśalamaśeṣata eva yacca prajñāprayogaviṣayo 'ṣṭavikalpa eṣaḥ // Ps_6.54 //
children.translated_text: and in all <s>dharmas</s> without exception — this eightfold analysis is the domain of the application of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom). Ps_6.54

children.text: niḥsāraphenanicayairaviśeṣi rūpaṃ tisro 'pi budbudalavā iva vedanāśca /
children.translated_text: <s>Rūpa</s> (form) is indistinguishable from heaps of insubstantial foam; the three types of <s>vedanā</s> (feeling) are like water bubbles;

children.text: saṃjñāpi kāmaguṇaviprasṛtān satṛṣṇān bālān mṛgāniva vilobhayate marīciḥ // Ps_6.55 //
children.translated_text: <s>Saṃjñā</s> (perception) too, like a mirage, deceives the foolish beings who are thirsty and drawn toward sensual pleasures, as deer are deceived. Ps_6.55

children.text: saṃskārajātirapi tulyaguṇā kadalyā vijñānato 'pi na ca yuktatarāsti māyā /
children.translated_text: The class of <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations) is equal in nature to the plantain tree; and no illusion (<s>māyā</s>) is more fitting than <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness),
depending on which the body, resembling a corpse possessed by spirits, wanders about with manifold conceptual activities. Ps_6.56

children.text: nātmā tadīyamapi cātra na kiṃ cid asti saṃghāta eṣa vividhāśūcisaṃnidhānaḥ /
children.translated_text: There is no <s>ātman</s> (self), nor is there anything belonging to it here — this is merely an aggregate, a collection of various impurities;

children.text: bālān pralambhayata eva ca sattvasaṃjñā svacchandaceṣṭa iva yantravidhau suyukte // Ps_6.57 //
children.translated_text: yet the notion of a being (<s>sattvasaṃjñā</s>) deceives the foolish, as if a mechanism well-constructed acts of its own accord. Ps_6.57

children.text: ātmā na cakṣurapi ca kṣaṇabhaṅguratvāt tadvan na cakṣuṣi na cātra yathaiva cakṣuḥ /
children.translated_text: The self is not the eye, for that too is momentary and perishable; nor is the self in the eye, nor is it like the eye;

children.text: ādhyātmikāyatanaśeṣam aśeṣam evam ātmīyavastuviṣayo 'pi ca tadvivekī // Ps_6.58 //
children.translated_text: thus for all the remaining internal <s>āyatanas</s> (sense bases) without exception — such is the discernment regarding the domain of what is called 'one's own.' Ps_6.58

children.text: bāhyeṣu dhātuṣu śarīrasamāśritānāṃ nālpo 'pi lakṣaṇavirodhakṛto 'sti bhedaḥ /
children.translated_text: Between the external <s>dhātus</s> (elements) and those residing in the body, there is not even the slightest distinction that creates a contradiction of characteristics;

children.text: vijñānadhāturapi ca kṣaṇikaḥ sa nātmā tasmātparo 'pi ca nabhaḥkusumaiḥ samānaḥ // Ps_6.59 //
children.translated_text: and the <s>vijñāna-dhātu</s> (consciousness element) too is momentary — it is not the self; therefore what is beyond that is also like a flower in the sky. Ps_6.59

children.text: ityetadudbhavati kevalameva duḥkhaṃ tṛṣṇāvimūḍhamanaso vigmāttu tasyāḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus, this suffering alone arises, of one whose mind is deluded by <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving); but from the cessation of that craving,

children.text: śāntiḥ parā bhavati tarṣaharastu mārgaḥ śīlaṃ samādhipariśuddhatayā ca dṛṣṭiḥ // Ps_6.60 //
children.translated_text: supreme peace comes about; the path is what removes that thirst — <s>śīla</s> (moral conduct) and <s>dṛṣṭi</s> (right view) purified through <s>samādhi</s> (concentration). Ps_6.60

children.text: tattatpratītya bhavatīti viśuddhadṛṣṭirnāstyasti veti samupaiti sa naiva kiṃ cit /
children.translated_text: One of pure vision, seeing that each thing arises in dependence on that, does not at all arrive at 'it exists' or 'it does not exist';

children.text: māyāmayaṃ jagadidaṃ pratibhāti tasya tasmāt sukhādiṣu bhavatyavikāradhīraḥ // Ps_6.61 //
children.translated_text: this world appears to such a one as if made of illusion (<s>māyā</s>); therefore, regarding pleasure and the like, one remains steadfast and undisturbed. Ps_6.61

children.text: āsīdbhaviṣyati ca yat tad apīdṛgeva kaḥ saṃbhavo yadasukhaṃ na bhaved bhavebhyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Whatever was and whatever will be is also of this very same nature — what possibility is there that suffering would not arise from existences?

children.text: evaṃ vyatītaviṣayeṣvapi vītarāgo naivābhinandati bhavāṃśca bhaviṣyato 'pi // Ps_6.62 //
children.translated_text: Thus, free from attachment even regarding past objects, one does not delight in future existences either. Ps_6.62
Who would become attached to a person who is an offender, harsh in the variety of his appearances, with the marks of hidden claws and exposed fangs clearly visible,

children.text: tatpraiṣyavṛttikapaṭānyanucintya rajyed viśvāsameva ca yathocitamatra yāyāt // Ps_6.63 //
children.translated_text: upon reflecting on his servant-like deceitful conduct, and would place trust in such a one as appropriate? Ps_6.63
Thus, though one of liberated mind, yet being compassionate, seeing the world helpless and caught within the folds of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions),

children.text: hīneṣu niṣpraṇayabuddhirudārabhāvān nirvātumicchati na buddhaguṇānalabdhvā // Ps_6.64 //
children.translated_text: with noble dispositions, unwilling in thought toward the inferior, one does not wish to depart into <s>nirvāṇa</s> without having attained the qualities of a <s>Buddha</s>. Ps_6.64
Having cast aside, from the very beginning, the two vehicles (<s>yānadvaya</s>) that are insufficient in form for accomplishing the welfare of the world,
one has mounted the vehicle of the king of sages (<s>munirājayāna</s>), the path taught through compassion (<s>kāruṇya</s>), whose very nature is sole devotion to the benefit of others. Ps_6.65

children.text: hīnociteṣu na matirnamati praṇītā saṃtiṣṭhate mahati nāmahatī kadā cit /
children.translated_text: A noble mind does not incline toward what befits the inferior; a small mind never abides in what is great;

children.text: saṃsyandate śucibhireva śucisvabhāvaṃ tulyaistathānyadapi śāsvata eṣa yogaḥ // Ps_6.66 //
children.translated_text: what is pure by nature flows only with the pure — likewise with equals; this is the eternal law (<s>yoga</s>). Ps_6.66

children.text: svapnopamāni vigaṇayya sukhāsukhāni saṃmohadoṣakṛpaṇāṃ janatāṃ ca teṣu /
children.translated_text: Reckoning pleasures and pains as dreamlike, and seeing the people wretched through the fault of delusion in those very things,

children.text: ātmārtha eva gurutāṃ katham asya yāyād vyāpārabhāramavadhūya parārtharamyam // Ps_6.67 //
children.translated_text: how could self-interest assume importance for such a one, when the charm of working for others has cast off the burden of concern? Ps_6.67
One whose every effort is directed toward the welfare of all the world, who has abandoned the false conceit that is the domain of self-view (<s>ātmadṛṣṭi</s>),

children.text: sarvatra śāntamatiradvayamārgacārī so 'tyadbhutaścaritanirvṛta eva loke // Ps_6.68 //
children.translated_text: whose mind is peaceful everywhere, who walks the non-dual path — that one is truly wondrous, finding fulfillment (<s>nirvṛta</s>) in the world itself. Ps_6.68
This supreme vehicle (<s>uttamayāna</s>), which brings about the purification of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) — <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience) is indeed the arising from it of the great sages;

children.text: lokasya yā nayanatāmiva saṃprayāti dīptāṃśumaṇḍalatalotpatitā prabheva // Ps_6.69 //
children.translated_text: that which attains, as it were, the status of an eye for the world, like a radiance risen from the surface of the blazing solar disc. Ps_6.69
One who, though crushed by the weight of the faults of <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence), is never wearied through the discerning power of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom),

children.text: nātmābhikhedapariviklavatāṃ sa yāti yānasya buddhaguṇasaṃjananasya loke // Ps_6.70 //
children.translated_text: does not fall into the distress of self-torment in this world, for the sake of the vehicle that generates the qualities of a <s>Buddha</s>. Ps_6.70
And those who behold the wondrous power of the <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone One), every part of their bodies bristling with hair standing on end,

children.text: tadgāminaṃ pariharanti ca yānamārgaṃ kiṃ nāma kāraṇamṛte śaṭhaceṣṭitebhyaḥ // Ps_6.71 //
children.translated_text: yet turn away from the vehicle-path leading to that — what reason could there be for this, other than deceitful conduct? Ps_6.71
Who, unless their mind is overcome by the defilements of <s>Māra</s>, could revile the vehicle of <s>sarvajña</s> (omniscience),

children.text: sarvajñayānamapayānam anarthapaṅkād ākroṣṭumarhati na cejjagato 'sya vairam // Ps_6.72 //
children.translated_text: which is the treasury of the jewels of the qualities of the <s>dharma</s> of a <s>sambuddha</s> (fully awakened one), and a vessel of deliverance from the mire of misfortune — unless they are hostile to the world? Ps_6.72
When those of the lineage of the king of <s>Jinas</s>, devoted to accomplishing the welfare of the world, with eyes closed by <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), stumble,

children.text: cittaṃ narasya karuṇāmṛdu kasya na syāt tanmohadoṣaśamanāya dṛḍhaṃ ca vīryam // Ps_6.73 //
children.translated_text: whose heart would not become tender with <s>karuṇā</s> (compassion), and whose valor firm, for the pacification of the fault of their delusion? Ps_6.73

children.text: prajñāyā janayati yaḥ parāṃ viśuddhiṃ nirmokṣaḥ kathamiva tasya dūrataḥ syāt /
children.translated_text: He who produces the supreme purification of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) — how could liberation (<s>nirmokṣa</s>) be far from him?

children.text: naivāsmātparataramasti śīlam anyat tattasmād bhajata vimokṣakāṅkṣiṇo hi // Ps_6.74 //
children.translated_text: There is no other discipline (<s>śīla</s>) higher than this — therefore, O you who desire liberation (<s>vimokṣa</s>), cultivate it! (Ps_6.74)
Thus concludes the <s>Prajñā-pāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom) [chapter], and this is the <s>Pāramitāsamāsa</s> (Compendium of the Perfections).
From the lotuses of the <s>sūtrānta</s> (discourses) born in the lake of the pure mind of the Lord of Sages (<s>Munīndra</s>, the <s>Buddha</s>),
the bee named <s>Śūra</s> (<s>Āryaśūra</s>), having rightly gathered [nectar], has composed this <s>Pāramitāsamāsa</s>, rich with the honey [of the <s>Dharma</s>].
